# Mike Automations: full text

> Automation for small accounting and bookkeeping firms: document chasing, reminders and follow-ups, live in 2-3 days. Pay once you're happy with it.

Updated: 2026-11-10. Facts summary: https://mikeautomations.github.io/llms.txt

## Home: Mike Automations
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/

Automation for small accounting and bookkeeping firms: document chasing, reminders and follow-ups, live in 2-3 days. Pay once you're happy with it.

- Workflow automation: $2,000. Paid once it's running and you're happy with it. A whole process, automated end to end. For example: collecting every client's records before the Self Assessment deadline, from first request to filed, or chasing VAT paperwork every quarter.
- Custom system: From $5,000. One-time, by scope. Clients, jobs, documents and tasks in one place. Everyone sees what's due today.
- Monthly support: $150/mo. Optional. Cancel with 30 days' notice. Hosting, monitoring and small changes, by the person who built it.

## Frequently asked questions
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/faq/

### What does "pay when you're happy" mean?
We write down what the workflow has to do, such as "every new client gets a checklist and reminders until their documents are in." It goes live in your firm, you check it, and if it does that and you're happy with it, you pay. If not, you don't. There's no deposit.

### How much does it cost?
Workflow automation is $2,000. The first 3 firms get it for $1,500. Custom systems start at $5,000, and optional monthly support is $150. Prices in US dollars, invoiced in $, £ or € at the equivalent rate. The pricing page compares the three side by side.

### How long does it take?
The written plan comes within 48 hours of the call. The build usually takes 2-3 days. From the call to live is usually under a week, and you pay once you're happy with it.

### Who will I work with?
Michael, and only Michael. Mike Automations is one person: the person on your first call maps your process, builds the workflow and supports it afterwards. No account managers and no hand-offs.

### Do I need to be technical?
No. You show me how you do it today, and I build it. The walkthrough is in plain English, and you get a one-page guide.

### Will this replace Xero, QuickBooks or our portal?
No. It works with what you have, including portals like Karbon or TaxDome. It just does the chasing and the copying.

### Which tools does it work with?
Xero, QuickBooks, FreeAgent, Sage, Gmail, Outlook, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Karbon, TaxDome, Slack and more. If yours isn't listed, ask. Most tools have a way in.

### Do you use AI?
Only where it helps, for example to read an email or sort an upload. A person always approves anything AI prepares before it goes to a client, and you approve the wording of every message first.

### What about client data and GDPR?
It stays in your accounts: your email, your drive, your tools. I only get the access the workflow needs, and I don't use the data for anything else. Details in the privacy policy.

### Will my clients know it's automated?
They'll see friendly emails written in your voice and sent from your address. You approve the wording before anything goes out.

### What if something breaks?
In the first weeks live, I'm watching it closely and fix anything straight away. Small fixes are included for 60 days after go-live. After that, support is optional at $150/month, or I quote any fix before doing it.

### Can I pause or turn it off?
Yes. Every build has a simple off switch, and the one-page guide shows where it is.

### Who owns what you build?
You do. It runs in your accounts. If we stop working together, it keeps running, and I hand over everything you need.

### Where are you based?
I'm Michael, a native English speaker. I'm based in Haifa, Israel, and I work remotely with small firms in the UK, US, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Europe, on UK hours. Calls are Monday to Thursday, 2-6 PM UK time (usually 9 AM-1 PM in New York). Everything else is by email. The Sheffield address on this site is a UK mailing address for post only. It isn't an office.

### Can it be ready before the January deadline?
Yes. The build takes 2-3 days. Start in November and it's chasing records well before 31 January.

### Do you work with firms outside the UK?
Yes: the UK, US, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Europe. Everything is in English, and invoices are in $, £ or €.

### What happens on the 15-minute call?
You tell me what eats your week. I ask a few questions and tell you straight whether it's worth automating. No pitch. If it fits, the written plan follows within 48 hours.

## Services (Mike Automations): Workflow automation services: the admin that eats your week, done for you.
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/services/

Mike Automations offers workflow automation services for small accounting, bookkeeping and service firms: the chasing, reminders, follow-ups and copying between tools, done for you on the tools you already use. Mike Automations is one person, Michael, who builds one workflow automation for a fixed $2,000 ($1,500 for the first 3 firms), live in 2-3 days, and you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it. Bigger jobs become a custom system, from $5,000.
We build it. It runs. Then you pay.

### Workflow automation: $2,000
A whole process, automated end to end, from the first request to done. Typical workflows:
- Document collection each client gets a personal checklist, reminders go out until it's in, and files land in the right folder.
- Client onboarding engagement letter, ID checks, first documents and welcome email, all in order.
- Follow-ups quotes, invoices and approvals get a polite nudge until someone answers.
- Morning summary one short list of who's still missing what.
- Paid once it's running, does what the written plan says, and you're happy with it.

### Custom system: from $5,000
When spreadsheets and email threads stop being enough. Clients, jobs, documents and tasks in one place, and everyone sees what's due today.
- A web app with a login per person. Works on your phone.
- Your existing spreadsheets moved over.
- First version live in 3-4 weeks, plus 60 days of fixes.
- AI only where it helps, and a person always signs off.

### AI agents, with a person in charge
Some steps need reading, not just copying: sorting an email, checking which document a client uploaded, or drafting a reply. An AI step can do that part. A person always approves anything AI prepares before it reaches a client, and nothing is sent without wording you've approved.

### Monthly support: $150/month, optional
Hosting, monitoring and small changes, by the person who built it. Cancel with 30 days' notice.

### What every build includes
- A free 15-minute call, then a written plan with a fixed price within 48 hours.
- A clear definition of "working", agreed before anything is built.
- A 30-minute walkthrough in plain English and a one-page guide.
- An off switch you can use any time.
- Small fixes are included for 60 days after go-live.
- It runs in your accounts, and you own it.

### Works with what you already use
Nothing to replace. If a tool isn't on the list, ask. Most have a way in.

### How "pay when you're happy" works
1. We agree in writing what the workflow must do. For example: "every new client gets a checklist and reminders until their documents are in."
2. It goes live in your firm on real work, and you check it.
3. If it does what the plan says and you're happy with it, you pay. If not, you owe nothing, and I remove anything you don't want to keep.

### What sets the price of a custom system
A custom system is priced by scope, in writing, before any work starts. These are the things that usually change the scope:
- How many people need a login, and what each of them should see.
- How many tools it connects to.
- How much data moves over from your spreadsheets.
- How many steps, approvals and reports the work involves.
- Whether any step needs AI to read or draft text.

### What's not included
- Licences for third-party tools you choose to add, such as a paid Zapier plan. We tell you about any of these before you agree, and most builds use tools you already pay for.
- New work beyond the written plan. Anything extra is quoted separately, and only goes ahead with your OK.

### Payment
Invoice in USD, GBP or EUR. Pay by bank transfer.

## How it works (Mike Automations): How an automation project works, from call to live.
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/

An automation project with Mike Automations runs in six steps: a free 15-minute call, a written plan with a fixed price within 48 hours, a build of usually 2-3 days, a 30-minute walkthrough, a live period on real work, and payment only once you're happy with it. From the call to live is usually under a week. Nothing starts until you accept the plan, and nothing goes to your clients until you've approved the wording.
We build it. It runs. Then you pay.

### The steps
- 1. A 15-minute call. You show me what eats your week. I ask how it's done today, what tools you use, and what "done" looks like. No preparation needed.
- 2. A written plan within 48 hours. What gets automated and what stays manual, which tools it connects to, how we'll know it works, and a fixed price. Nothing starts until you say yes.
- 3. The build, usually 2-3 days. I build it with your accounts and your tools. You get read-only access to see it take shape. Nothing goes out to clients until you've approved the wording.
- 4. A 30-minute walkthrough. A short session in plain English, plus a one-page guide: what it does, where to look, and how to pause it.
- 5. Live. It runs on real work. I watch it closely and fix anything that needs fixing.
- 6. You pay, when you're happy. If it does what the plan said and you're happy with it, you pay the fixed price. If not, you owe nothing.

### The timeline at a glance
Step | When | Your part
--- | --- | ---
Free call | Monday to Thursday, 2-6 PM UK time | 15 minutes
Written plan | Within 48 hours of the call | Read it, then say yes or no
Build | Usually 2-3 days | Approve the wording of any client message
Walkthrough | When the build is ready | 30 minutes
Live | On real work in your firm | Check it does what the plan says
Payment | Once it's running and you're happy with it | Pay the fixed price; the invoice is due within 14 days

### What the written plan contains
- What gets automated, and what stays manual.
- Which tools it connects to, and the access it needs.
- What "working" means, written as success criteria you can check. For example: "every client with items outstanding gets a reminder every 7 days until they're in."
- The fixed price, and anything not included, such as a paid licence for a tool you choose to add.
- When it goes live.

### Access and your data
It stays in your accounts: your email, your drive, your tools. I only get the access the workflow needs, and I don't use the data for anything else.
Because everything runs in your own accounts, you can remove my access at any time from your side.

### If you're not happy
You owe nothing for that build, and I remove anything you don't want to keep. The success criteria in the plan are what we both check against, so there's no argument about what "done" means.

### After go-live
- Small fixes are included for 60 days after go-live.
- Monthly support is optional at $150/month, and you can cancel with 30 days' notice.
- Every build has an off switch, and the one-page guide shows where it is.
- It's yours. If we stop working together, it keeps running, and I hand over everything you need.

### What you need to do
- Join one 15-minute call and one 30-minute walkthrough.
- Give access to the tools the workflow needs, and only those.
- Approve the wording of any message that goes to your clients.

## About (Mike Automations): Hi, I'm Michael Gershman.
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/about/

I'm Michael Gershman, and Mike Automations is me: one person who maps how a small firm works, then builds and supports the automations, custom systems and AI agents that take its repetitive admin off its plate. I'm a native English speaker. I'm based in Haifa, Israel, and I work remotely with small firms in the UK, US, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Europe, on UK hours. Every build has a fixed price, and you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it.

### The short version
Mike Automations is one person, Michael, who builds one workflow automation for a fixed $2,000 ($1,500 for the first 3 firms), live in 2-3 days, and you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it.
No account managers and no hand-offs. The person you talk to on the first call is the person who builds your workflow and looks after it.

### Where I work
I'm based in Haifa, Israel, and I work remotely with small firms in the UK, US, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Europe, on UK hours. Calls are Monday to Thursday, 2-6 PM UK time (usually 9 AM-1 PM in New York). Everything else is by email, and you'll usually hear back the same working day.
The Sheffield address on this site is a UK mailing address for post only. It isn't an office.

### What I do
Most small firms don't need new software. They need the repetitive part done for them: the chasing, the reminders, the copying from one tool to another. Those jobs are dull, they eat hours every week, and they are exactly what automation is good at.
- Workflow automation one whole process automated end to end, such as collecting every client's records before a deadline. $2,000, live in 2-3 days.
- Custom systems clients, jobs, documents and tasks in one place, when spreadsheets stop being enough. From $5,000.
- AI agents an AI step that reads, sorts or drafts, with a person approving anything it prepares.
- What you buy is a result, such as "every client gets a checklist and reminders until their documents are in", not a piece of technology.

### How a project runs
1. A free 15-minute call. You show me what eats your week, and I tell you straight whether it's worth automating.
2. A written plan with a fixed price within 48 hours: what gets automated, what stays manual, and how we'll know it works.
3. The build, usually 2-3 days, on your accounts and your tools.
4. A 30-minute walkthrough and a one-page guide.
5. It runs on real work. If it does what the plan says and you're happy with it, you pay.

### Why one person maps, builds and supports
Because nothing gets lost between the person who listened and the person who builds. The person who mapped your process is the one who fixes it if something changes, and you never have to explain your firm twice.

### Why a fixed price, and why you pay when you're happy
You're buying a result, not my time, so the price is fixed in writing before any work starts. And because you only pay once it's running in your firm and you're happy with it, the risk sits with me, not with you. There's no deposit and no hourly billing.

### What I won't do
- Lock you in. It runs in your accounts and you own it. If we stop working together, it keeps running, and I hand over everything you need.
- Let AI act on its own. A person always approves anything AI prepares, and you approve the wording of every client message first.
- Sell you software you don't need. I build on the tools you already use.
- Ask for more access than the workflow needs, or use your data for anything else.
- Bill by the hour, or ask for a deposit.

## Accountants (UK) (Mike Automations): Automation for UK accounting practices: deadline season, minus the chasing.
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/accountants/

Automation for UK accounting practices takes the chasing off your team: every client gets a personal checklist for Self Assessment, VAT, year-end or payroll records, reminders go out on their own until it's in, and you get a morning list of who's still outstanding. It's built on the practice software and email you already use, live in 2-3 days, for a fixed $2,000 that you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it.
It's for small UK accounting and bookkeeping practices. We build it. It runs. Then you pay.

### The problem
Every January, someone at your practice spends hours emailing clients for the same P60s, bank statements and receipts. Then the same again for VAT every quarter, for each company's year end, and for MTD quarterly updates too. Nobody trained as an accountant to send "just a gentle reminder" forty times.

### Every deadline, one way of chasing
The same workflow handles each deadline your clients have. The dates below are from gov.uk, checked in November 2026.
- Self Assessment HMRC says online returns for the 2025-26 tax year must be in by 11:59pm on 31 January 2027. Each client gets their own records list from the autumn, with reminders that speed up in January.
- VAT quarters HMRC says VAT returns are usually due one calendar month and 7 days after the end of each VAT period. Requests go out before each quarter end, with a short list of unexplained bank-feed items.
- Company year ends Companies House says private companies have 9 months after the end of their accounting period to file accounts. Requests follow each company's own year end, so the chasing is spread across the year.
- MTD for Income Tax quarterly reminders for clients already signed up, so records come in every quarter, not once a year.
- Payroll starters, leavers and changes requested before each pay run.
- Your own fees polite invoice reminders that stop the moment a client pays.

### What gets automated
- Checklists per client built from what each client needs: Self Assessment, VAT, year-end or payroll.
- Reminders until it's in friendly emails in your voice, from your address, at sensible intervals. They stop as soon as the upload arrives.
- Files in the right folder each upload lands in the client's folder and gets checked off.
- Morning list who's still outstanding, and what for. One email, before you start.
- Optional extras engagement letters drafted from what came in, AML ID checks requested and tracked, and MTD quarterly reminders.

### What stays with you
- Reviewing the records and preparing the returns.
- Advice, judgement calls and anything a client should hear from you.
- Approving engagement letters, AML decisions and the wording of every client email.

### Works with
Already using a portal? It stays. This adds the chasing on top.

### Price
$2,000, or $1,500 for the first 3 firms. Prices in US dollars, invoiced in $, £ or € at the equivalent rate. Paid once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Timing
The build takes 2-3 days. Start in November, and it's chasing records well before 31 January.

## Agencies (Mike Automations): Workflow automation for agencies: less waiting on clients.
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agencies/

Workflow automation for agencies chases clients for you: every new client gets a checklist of logins, assets and access, reminders go out until each item arrives, drafts get a nudge until they're approved, and each morning you see who's holding up which project. It's built on the tools your team already uses, live in 2-3 days, for a fixed $2,000 that you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it.
It suits small marketing, design, web and creative agencies. We build it. It runs. Then you pay.

### The problem
Most agencies lose more time waiting on clients than doing the work. The logins, the brand assets, the copy, the feedback round, the final sign-off. Then a project manager spends half the week sending "just checking in" emails, and deadlines slip anyway.

### What gets automated
- Onboarding checklist each new client gets a short list of exactly what you need, such as logins, assets, brand guide and access, with one place to upload.
- Reminders until it's in polite nudges in your voice. They stop when the item arrives.
- Approvals and sign-offs a draft goes out, a reminder follows if there's no answer, and the approval is logged.
- "Waiting on client" board one morning list of who's holding up which project, and for how long.
- Hand-offs when a client delivers, the right person is told, in Slack, email or your project tool.
- Invoices polite payment reminders that stop the moment the client pays.

### Approvals without the chasing
A draft is ready. Here's how the approval can run on its own:
- Example reminder: "Hi Jo, just a quick one: are you happy for us to go ahead with the homepage draft we sent on Tuesday? A yes or a list of changes is all we need. Thanks, Sam"
1. The draft goes to the client with one clear question: approve, or send changes.
2. No answer after 2 working days? A short reminder goes out in the account manager's name.
3. Still nothing after 4 working days? The account manager gets a heads-up to call.
4. The answer is logged against the project, and the right person is told.

### What you see each morning
- Project A: waiting 3 days for the domain login.
- Project B: homepage draft sent, no reply yet, reminder went out yesterday.
- Project C: everything in, ready to start.

### What stays with you
- The creative work and the client relationship.
- Calls, and any conversation about scope or budget.
- The wording of every message, approved by you once before it runs.

### Works with

### Price

Automation for small service businesses handles the follow-up that slips when you're busy: every enquiry gets a reply within minutes and goes on one list, customers get a reminder before their appointment, happy customers get a review request, and unpaid invoices get polite reminders. It's for UK clinics, salons, cleaners, gardeners, letting agents and other small service businesses. US home service contractors have their own page for estimate follow-up.

### The problem
An enquiry comes in while you're with a customer. A customer forgets the appointment. A happy customer never leaves a review. An invoice sits unpaid because nobody had time to chase it. None of these takes long, but they all slip when you're busy, and every one costs money.

- Appointment reminders the day before, by email or text, with an easy way to reschedule.
- Review requests after the job, a polite ask with a direct link to your Google reviews.
- Invoice reminders a friendly note before the due date and on the day, stopping the moment they pay.
- Weekly summary enquiries in, jobs booked, reviews asked for and invoices still open.

### By type of business

- Salons booking reminders, and a clear deposit and cancellation policy sent with every booking.

## Examples (Mike Automations): Automation examples: what a build looks like.
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/examples/

These four automation examples show what a typical Mike Automations build does, step by step: a Self Assessment records chase for a UK practice, new-client onboarding for an agency, quote follow-up for a home services contractor, and VAT quarter paperwork for a bookkeeper. They are illustrations made with demo data, not client stories. Names, numbers and firms are invented.

### Example 1: Self Assessment records chase (accounting practice, UK)
The situation (illustrative): a five-person practice with around 300 Self Assessment clients, chasing records by hand from October to January.
- What stays manual: reviewing the documents and preparing the return.
1. On 1 October, every client gets a personal checklist: P60, bank statements, rental income and so on, depending on their file.
2. Reminders go out every 7 days, then every 3 days in January. They stop when the upload arrives.
3. Each upload is filed to Clients/{Name}/2025-26/ and ticked off.
4. Every morning at 8:30, the partners get one email: who's outstanding, what's missing, and how many days are left.

### Example 2: New-client onboarding (digital agency)
The situation (illustrative): a small web agency where each new project stalls for one to two weeks waiting for logins and assets.
1. The contract is signed, and the client gets a welcome email with a short checklist: domain login, brand files, copy and access to analytics.
2. One upload link. Each item is ticked off as it arrives.
3. A reminder goes out after 3 days, and another after 6. On day 8 the account manager gets a heads-up.
4. When everything is in, the project moves to "Ready to start" in the project tool, and the team is told in Slack.

### Example 3: Quote follow-up (home services contractor)
The situation (illustrative): a three-van plumbing business that sends 20-30 quotes a month and rarely follows up.
1. Every quote sent is logged automatically.
2. On day 2 and day 5, a short friendly follow-up goes out in the owner's name. It stops the moment the customer replies.
3. Replies go straight to the owner's phone.
4. Every Monday: quotes sent, won and still open.

### Example 4: VAT quarter paperwork (bookkeeping firm)
The situation (illustrative): a bookkeeper with 60 VAT-registered clients on quarterly returns.
1. Two weeks before each quarter end, every VAT client gets a request for invoices, receipts and bank statements.
2. If the bank feed in Xero shows uncategorised transactions, the client gets a short list to explain.
3. The bookkeeper gets a dashboard: ready to file, waiting on client, or overdue.

## Automation for US bookkeepers and tax preparers: stop chasing W-2s and 1099s
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bookkeepers/

Automation for US bookkeepers and tax preparers means the tax-season chasing runs on its own: each client gets their own list of missing W-2s, 1099s and receipts, an upload link, and reminders until the list is complete. Signed engagement letters and Form 8879s are chased the same way. You still review every return and make every call.

Automation for bookkeepers and tax preparers starts with the part of busy season that isn't accounting at all. Most of January to April goes to [emailing clients for missing W-2s and 1099s](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/tax-season-client-email-calendar/), digging receipts out of texts, chasing signatures and keeping a mental list of who still owes you what. That part can run on its own, on the tools you already use, while you spend your hours on the returns.

### The dates that drive tax season
Your clients can't send what they haven't received yet, so the chasing should follow the IRS calendar. For 2026 wages, the IRS General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026) say employers must give employees their W-2s by February 1, 2027, the same day the forms are due at the Social Security Administration. The IRS Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (12/2026) say Form 1099-NEC is due by January 31, and a date that falls on a weekend moves to the next business day, which is also February 1, 2027. The same instructions say the reporting threshold for many payments, including nonemployee compensation, rose from $600 to $2,000 for tax years beginning after 2025. Clients who pay contractors will ask you about that, so it belongs in your first email of the season. Our [1099-NEC checklist for bookkeepers](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/1099-season-checklist-bookkeepers/) covers the rest.

### A tax-season chasing timeline you can copy
When | What goes out | Who it's for
--- | --- | ---
Early November | Engagement letter for the new season, plus a short info form | Every returning client
Mid-December | W-9 request for anyone your business clients paid this year | Business clients who file 1099s
Early January | Each client's own checklist and an upload link | Every client
February 2 | "Your W-2s and 1099s should have arrived" reminder, listing only what's missing | Clients who aren't complete
Late February | Second reminder, and your list of who needs a personal call | Clients still missing items
When the return is ready | Form 8879 for e-file signature, with reminders until it's signed | Clients whose return is ready
Mid-March | Extension conversation: what's missing and the plan | Clients still incomplete

### What an automated tax-season workflow takes off your plate
- A personal checklist for every client, [built from last year's return](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/tax-organizer-questions-new-vs-returning-clients/): the W-2s, 1099s, mortgage statements and receipts you expect from them
- Reminders by email (and text, if you want it) that list only what's still missing, and stop the moment the list is complete
- One upload link per client: every file is renamed, saved in the right client folder and ticked off
- [W-9 collection](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/w9-request-email-template/) for business clients who file their own 1099s. The IRS calls Form W-9 the "Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification"
- Signature chasing for engagement letters and Form 8879, which the IRS describes as the signature authorization for a return e-filed by an electronic return originator (ERO)
- A morning summary of who's complete, who's partial and who hasn't opened anything

### A first-of-season email you can use
Early January checklist email (edit the list per client):
```
Subject: Your 2026 tax documents: what we need from you

Hi [First name],

It's time to start your 2026 return. Based on last year, this is what we need from you:

- W-2 from [Employer]
- 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC from [Payer], if you received one
- 1099-INT from [Bank]
- Mortgage interest statement (Form 1098)
- Receipts for [deductible items you discussed]

Employers and payers have until February 1, 2027 to send W-2s, 1099-NECs and 1099-MISCs, so some of these may not have arrived yet. Upload each one here when you have it: [upload link]

If something on this list doesn't apply to you this year, just reply and tell us. We'll only remind you about what's still missing.

Thanks,
[Your name]
```

### What stays with you
Everything that needs your judgment. The workflow requests, collects, files and reminds. You decide what goes on each checklist, review the return, make the calls and sign off. If AI drafts a message to a client, a person always approves it before it goes out. For the month-end side of the work (bank statements, receipts and invoices every month or quarter), see the client document collection workflow page.

We start with a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how documents come in today and where the chasing happens. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every client gets their checklist on January 5 and reminders stop when they're complete". It's built on the tools you already use: QuickBooks, TaxDome or Karbon, Gmail or Outlook, Google Drive or Dropbox. Your team doesn't learn a new system. It goes live in 2-3 days, costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Can it be ready before tax season?
Yes. The workflow is built in 2-3 days. If we start in November or December, it's live well before the first W-2s go out.

Yes. It sends the document from your e-signature tool, reminds the client on a schedule and stops when it's signed. You still prepare and review the 8879 yourself.

## Estimate follow-up automation for home service contractors
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/contractors/

Estimate follow-up automation sends every open estimate a short, polite follow-up on a fixed schedule, by email or text, until the customer says yes or no, and gives you a daily list of the ones worth a phone call. For a home service contractor it usually also covers appointment reminders and logging every new lead in one list. You still set the prices and make the calls.

Estimate follow-up automation fixes the most common leak in a remodeling, [HVAC](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/hvac-maintenance-agreement-renewals/), plumbing or [cleaning business](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/cleaning-business-automation/). You send an estimate, the customer says they'll think about it, and then nobody calls back because you're on the next job. Meanwhile [appointments get forgotten](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reduce-appointment-no-shows/) and someone drives across town to an empty house. A workflow can do the remembering, from estimate to booked job, built on the software you already have.

### An estimate follow-up schedule you can copy
An estimate that goes quiet isn't always a no. Often the customer got busy, is comparing two bids or has a question they didn't ask. A fixed schedule means every estimate gets the same polite attention, whoever wrote it.
When | What goes out | Channel
--- | --- | ---
Same day | The estimate, with one line on what happens next | Email
Day 2 | "Any questions about the estimate?" with your direct number | Text or email
Day 7 | A short note: what's included, how soon you can start | Email
Day 14 | "Should I keep this open for you?" (easy to answer yes or no) | Text
Day 30 | Estimate marked closed, and you get a note to call if it's a big job | Internal

### A follow-up text you can use
Day 2 text (edit the wording; it goes out from your business number):
```
Hi [First name], it's [Your name] from [Business]. Just checking you got the estimate for the [job] at [street]. Happy to answer any questions or walk through the options. Reply here or call me on [number]. Reply STOP to opt out.
```

### What an automated workflow does for a contractor
- Every estimate gets [follow-up emails and texts](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/estimate-follow-up-email-templates-contractors/) on the schedule above until you get a yes or a no, and stops the moment the customer replies
- Appointment reminders the day before, with an easy way to confirm or reschedule
- New leads from your website, email or phone get logged in one list, with nothing left in someone's head
- After the job: a thank-you, the invoice link and a request for a review
- A daily list of open estimates by value, and who needs a call from you

### When your field software is enough
If you run Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan or similar field service software, check its follow-up settings first. If it already chases estimates the way you want, turn that on and you may not need anything else. A custom workflow makes sense when the gaps are between tools: estimates written in one place, leads arriving in another, reminders nobody set up, and no single list of what's still open.

### Texting customers: what to set up first
Texts from a business system to US phones on a regular 10-digit number fall under A2P 10DLC registration. Twilio's documentation says anyone sending SMS from an application to the US over a 10DLC number must register a brand (your business) and a campaign (what the messages are for, and how customers opt in and opt out). Twilio's fee page, checked in November 2026, lists a one-time brand registration from $4.50, a $15 campaign vetting fee and a monthly campaign fee from $1.50, plus per-message carrier fees. Other texting providers set their own prices. I set the registration up with you, and until it's approved the same follow-up runs by email.

### What stays with you
The pricing, the customer relationship and the work itself. The workflow does the remembering and the follow-up. You decide what to quote, which estimates are worth a call and what every message says.

### How Mike Automations builds it
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) to see where jobs slip today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every estimate gets the day 2, 7 and 14 follow-ups, and you get a daily list of open ones". It's built on what you already use (your email, calendar, Google Sheets or your field software), so there's nothing new to learn. It goes live in 2-3 days, costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Do reminders go out by text?
They can. Business texting to US phones on a regular number needs A2P 10DLC registration through your texting provider, which I set up with you. Email works from day one.

### We already use field service software. Does this replace it?
No. It connects to what you have and fills the gaps, like estimates your software doesn't chase or leads that arrive outside it.

### Won't customers find the follow-ups pushy?
Not if there are only a few, they're short and they stop the moment someone replies. You approve the wording and the schedule before anything goes live.

### What about calls I miss while I'm on a job?
That's a separate workflow: a missed call text back that logs the lead and books the estimate. It can feed straight into this follow-up list.

## How UK accountants automate Self Assessment document chasing
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/self-assessment-document-chasing/

Self Assessment document chasing is the work of getting each client's P60s, rental figures, pension statements and other records in before the 31 January online filing deadline. An automated chasing workflow sends every client their own list of what is still missing, reminds them on a schedule you set, stops as soon as they are complete, and gives you one daily list of who is still outstanding.

Self Assessment document chasing is the one job every UK practice repeats each autumn, and it peaks in January. The returns aren't hard, but half your clients still haven't sent [their P60, their rental figures or their pension statements](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/self-assessment-records-checklist-for-clients/), and the chasing eats the weeks you need for the actual work. That chasing is a process with fixed dates, so it can run on its own while you prepare returns.

### The Self Assessment dates your chasing has to beat
These are HMRC's dates for the 2025 to 2026 tax year, which ended on 5 April 2026 (gov.uk, "Self Assessment tax returns: deadlines", checked November 2026). [Your own cut-off for records](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/when-to-start-chasing-self-assessment-clients/) should sit well before 31 January, so there is time to prepare, review and get the return approved.
Date | What HMRC needs | What it means for chasing
--- | --- | ---
5 October 2026 | New clients must have told HMRC they need to file (registered for Self Assessment) | Check new clients are registered before you chase their records
31 October 2026 | Paper returns must reach HMRC | Clients still on paper need their records in by early October
30 December 2026 | Online returns, if the client wants the bill collected through their tax code | A natural cut-off for employed clients with small amounts owed
31 January 2027 | Online returns, and payment of the tax owed | Records should be in well before this, so returns can be reviewed and approved

### What a late return costs your client
HMRC's penalties page (gov.uk, "Self Assessment tax returns: penalties", checked November 2026) sets out what happens if the return is late: an initial £100 penalty; after 3 months, £10 a day up to £900; after 6 months, a further 5% of the tax due or £300, whichever is greater; after 12 months, another 5% or £300. Paying late brings separate penalties of 5% of the unpaid tax at 30 days, 6 months and 12 months, plus interest. The penalty falls on the client, but the stress, the appeals and the awkward conversation land on the practice.

### Why Self Assessment chasing piles up in January
- Every client needs a different list: P60s and P11Ds for employees, income and expenses for sole traders, rent and mortgage interest for landlords
- Requests go out once in the autumn and then live in someone's head and inbox
- Documents arrive by email, WhatsApp and post, so nobody can see at a glance who is complete
- Clients who send half their records think they're done, and nobody notices until January

### What an automated chasing workflow does
1. Builds each client's list for this tax year from last year's return and your notes, so a landlord isn't asked for a P60 and an employee isn't asked for rent statements.
2. Sends the first request on the date you choose (for example the first week of October), with one secure upload link per client.
3. Ticks off each item as it arrives and saves it to the client's folder for the right tax year.
4. Reminds only the clients who still owe something, about [only the items still missing](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/clients-who-send-some-documents-but-not-all/), on your schedule (for example every 10 days from October, then weekly from 2 January).
5. Flags clients who haven't opened a single email, so a person can pick up the phone.
6. Sends you a short morning list: who's complete, who's missing what, and who is getting close to your cut-off.

### A reminder you can copy
Reminder email for a client who has sent some records but not all:
```
Subject: Your 2025-26 tax return: 2 items still missing

Hi [first name],

Thanks for the documents you've sent so far. To finish your 2025-26 Self Assessment return we still need:

1. Your P60 from [employer]
2. The annual rental statement from [letting agent]

You can upload them here: [upload link]

If we have everything by [your cut-off date], we can have your return ready for you to approve well before HMRC's 31 January deadline.

If you're not sure what something is, just reply and tell us.

Thanks,
[your name]
[practice name]
```

### How it works
We start with a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you request Self Assessment records today: where the client lists live, how documents arrive and who does the chasing. Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/) and a clear definition of "working", for example: every Self Assessment client gets their own list, reminders stop when they are complete, and you get a morning status list. It's built on the tools your practice already uses (your email, your practice management software or a shared drive, and your client list), so nobody learns a new system. It's live in 2-3 days, and you pay once it does what we agreed and you're happy with it.

### What stays with you
The return, the advice and every judgement call. The workflow requests, reminds and files. You decide what counts as complete and when a client gets a phone call instead of another email, and anything written to a client in your name follows wording you approved.

### Is it too late to start before 31 January?
The workflow is built in 2-3 days. Starting in November or December gives you most of January with it running. Starting later still helps with the last batch of stragglers.

### What about clients who post paper records?
When paper arrives, someone in the office ticks those items off the client's list and the reminders adjust. Clients can still post records; the workflow just stops asking for what you already have.

### Can it handle partnerships and trusts?
Yes, as long as you can say what each type of client needs to send. Each client type gets its own list and schedule from the same client list.

### Does it work with our practice management software?
It connects to the tools you already have where they allow it. On the call we check exactly what can be connected in your setup, and what is better left manual.

### What about client data and UK GDPR?
The data stays in your accounts: your email, your drive, your software. I only get the access the workflow needs, and the data is never used for anything else.

## A client document collection workflow for bookkeepers
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bookkeeper-document-collection/

A client document collection workflow is the routine a bookkeeper uses every month or quarter to get bank statements, receipts and invoices from clients: define what each client owes, request it on a fixed day, collect it in one place, follow up until it's complete, and report who's still missing what. Automating it means the requests, reminders and filing happen on their own, and you only step in for the clients who need a phone call.

A client document collection workflow decides what to ask each client for, when to ask again and where every file goes. Month end, quarter end and year end all start the same way: waiting for bank statements, [receipts and invoices](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/collect-receipts-from-bookkeeping-clients/). With a written workflow, that waiting runs on a schedule instead of from memory, and it works the same whether you use Xero or QuickBooks, Gmail or Outlook.

### The five steps of a document collection workflow
1. Define the list: for each client, which documents you need every month, every quarter and once a year. Write it down per client, not per firm.
2. Request: send each client their own list on a fixed day, for example the 1st working day of the month. One generic email to everyone gets ignored.
3. Collect in one place: [a single upload link per client](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/client-portal-vs-email-document-collection/) instead of email attachments, texts and photos spread over three inboxes.
4. Follow up: [reminders on a schedule](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/document-chasing-email-templates/) until the list is complete, then stop. Each reminder lists only what's still missing.
5. Report: one view of who's complete, who's partial and who hasn't responded, ready before you sit down to do the books.

### A monthly document checklist by client type
Start every client from one of these and adjust. Anything that already arrives through a bank feed in your accounting software comes off the list.
Client type | Every month | Every quarter or year
--- | --- | ---
Sole trader, card payments | Statements for accounts without a bank feed, receipts over your set amount | Mileage log, home office costs, loan statements
Small limited company or LLC | Sales invoices not raised in the software, supplier bills, expense receipts | Payroll reports, loan and finance statements, asset purchases
Shop or café | Till or POS reports, card processor statements, cash takings record | Stock count, equipment purchases
Landlord | Rent received, letting agent statements, repair invoices | Mortgage interest statement, insurance renewals
Contractor or tradesperson | Supplier invoices, fuel and materials receipts | Vehicle costs, subcontractor payment records

### A reminder you can copy
Month-end reminder (sent on the 5th to clients who aren't complete):
```
Subject: Still needed for [Month]: 2 items

Hi [First name],

Thanks for what you've sent so far. To finish your [Month] books we still need:

- [Bank] statement for [Month]
- Receipt for the [Supplier] payment of [amount] on [date]

You can upload them here: [upload link]

If something doesn't exist (for example, the account wasn't used), just reply "none" and we'll tick it off.

Thanks,
[Your name]
```

### Where it usually breaks
Most firms have the first step right and the rest done by hand. Requests go out late because someone has to write them. Files arrive in five different places. Follow-ups depend on whoever remembers. A client who sent four of five documents gets the same "please send your documents" email as one who sent nothing, which annoys the good ones. And there's no list of who's still missing what until someone builds one in a spreadsheet the night before a deadline.

### What automating it changes
- Requests go out on the same day every period without anyone writing them
- Each file is named the same way (for example "Client - 2026-10 - Bank statement"), saved in the right client folder and ticked off the list
- Reminders stop automatically when a client is complete, so nobody gets chased for something they already sent
- Partial senders get a reminder that [names only the missing items](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/clients-who-send-some-documents-but-not-all/)
- You start the day with a short list of who needs a personal call

### When you don't need automation yet
If you have a handful of clients and they mostly send on time, a shared checklist and a calendar reminder may be enough. Try that first. Automation earns its keep when you're writing the same chasing emails every month, or when files keep landing in the wrong place.

### How Mike Automations builds it
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how documents come in today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every client gets their list on the 1st and reminders stop when they're complete". It's built on what you already use (Xero or QuickBooks, Gmail or Outlook, Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox), so your team doesn't learn a new system. It goes live in 2-3 days, costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Do my clients need to install anything or create an account?
No. They get an email with their list and an upload link that works on a phone or a computer.

### Can it skip documents that already come through a bank feed?
Yes. Where a client's bank feed already comes into Xero or QuickBooks, that account comes off their list. For everything else, it asks for exactly what is missing.

### What if a client sends the wrong document?
You mark it on the list and the workflow asks again for the right one. A person always decides what counts as complete.

### We already have a client portal. Do we still need this?
Maybe not. If clients use the portal and someone checks it, keep it. The workflow helps when the portal exists but clients still email, text or forget, because it sends the per-client list and the reminders and can point people to the portal.

## Automated invoice payment reminders for service firms
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/

Automated invoice payment reminders are polite emails that go out on a fixed schedule before and after an invoice's due date, checking your accounting software first so they stop the moment the client pays. A good setup sends a note before the due date, two or three firmer reminders after it, and then hands the invoice to a person with a summary instead of sending yet another email.

Automated invoice payment reminders do the part of credit control nobody enjoys. Most late invoices aren't disputes: the client meant to pay, the email got buried, and nobody followed up because chasing money feels awkward. A reminder workflow does the polite, repetitive part on a schedule, so you only step in when a real conversation is needed. Taking a [deposit with the quote](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/how-to-ask-for-a-deposit-on-a-quote/) means there's less to chase in the first place.

### Why invoices go unpaid longer than they should
- Reminders depend on someone noticing an invoice is overdue and finding time to write
- The first nudge goes out weeks late, when the invoice is already old news
- Clients who have paid sometimes get chased anyway, because the payment hasn't been matched yet
- Nobody has one list of what's overdue, by how long, and who has already been asked
- The built-in reminders in invoicing software are often switched off, or send the same message every time

### A reminder schedule you can copy
Days are counted from the due date. Change the timing and tone to suit your clients; the point is that every step happens without anyone remembering to do it.
When | What goes out | Tone
--- | --- | ---
3 days before due | The invoice, the amount, the due date and a payment link | Friendly heads-up
3 days after due | A short note that the invoice is now overdue, with the link again | Polite, assumes it was missed
10 days after due | A reminder that asks the client to reply if there's a problem with the invoice | Clear and direct
21 days after due | No email. The invoice goes to your call list with every message already sent | A person takes over

### Reminder wording you can copy
Reminder 3 days after the due date:
```
Subject: Invoice [number] for [amount] is now overdue

Hi [first name],

A quick note that invoice [number] for [amount], due on [due date], is still showing as unpaid on our side.

You can pay it here: [payment link]

If you've already paid, thank you, and please ignore this. If something on the invoice isn't right, just reply and we'll sort it out.

Thanks,
[your name]
[business name]
```

### What a payment reminder workflow does
- Checks your accounting software before each message and stops as soon as the invoice is paid
- Sends from your own email address, with wording you approved for each step
- Skips clients on a payment plan or an agreed extension until the new date
- Hands long-overdue invoices to a person with a short summary, instead of sending yet another email
- Sends you a weekly list: what's due, what's overdue and what came in

### UK late payment rules worth knowing
Between businesses in the UK, gov.uk's guide "Late commercial payments: charging interest and debt recovery" (checked November 2026) says that if no payment date was agreed, payment is late 30 days after the customer gets the invoice or you deliver the work, whichever is later. You can claim statutory interest of 8% plus the Bank of England base rate, unless your contract sets a different rate, and a fixed sum for recovery costs: £40 on debts up to £999.99, £70 from £1,000 to £9,999.99 and £100 from £10,000. These rules apply to business customers, not consumers. The government introduced a Commercial Payments Bill to Parliament in May 2026 that would cap most payment terms at 60 days and make late payment interest mandatory; gov.uk says there will be a lead-in period before it comes into force, so check the current position before relying on it. In the US, put any late fee or interest terms in your contract and check your state's rules before you charge them.

### For accounting practices chasing their own fees
Practices that chase clients for records all year often let their own fees slide. The same workflow works for practice fees: reminders tied to your [engagement terms](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/engagement-letter-automation/), a pause while a client's return or accounts are still waiting on their records, and a monthly list of fees outstanding by client. This is separate from chasing clients for records, which has its own [workflow guides](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/guides/) on this site.

### How it works
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you invoice today and where payments stall. Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/) and a clear definition of "working", for example: no paid invoice is ever chased, and anything 21 days overdue is on your list with its history. It's built on the tools you already use (Xero or QuickBooks, Stripe if you take card payments, and your email), so clients get messages from your own address. It's live in 2-3 days, and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### What stays with you
The client relationship. You approve every message template before anything goes out, you decide when a reminder becomes a phone call, and you agree any payment plan, extension or interest charge yourself. If AI drafts a reply to a client, a person always approves it first.

### Will clients find automated reminders pushy?
The wording and timing are yours. You can start with a courteous note before the due date and keep later reminders short and polite.

### My invoicing software already sends reminders. Why add this?
If its reminders do what you need, keep them. The workflow helps when you want a schedule tied to your own rules, messages from your address, a handover to a person, or one list across tools.

### Can it handle retainers and recurring invoices?
Yes. Recurring invoices follow the same schedule, and the workflow can skip clients who pay by direct debit, ACH or card on file.

### Should the reminders add late payment interest automatically?
Usually not. Most firms keep interest as a decision a person makes, case by case. The workflow can work out the amount and put it on your list, and you choose whether to send a new invoice for it.

## Chasing year-end records from limited company clients, on time
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/limited-company-year-end-records/

Chasing year-end records from limited company clients means asking each director for bank statements, loan balances, stock and asset details once their company's own financial year closes, then following up until the file is complete. Because Companies House expects a private company's accounts 9 months after its year end, an automated workflow starts each request on the client's year end, not on one date for everyone, and warns you early about the files that will be tight.

Chasing year-end records from limited company clients never stops, because each client has their own year end. Records drift in whenever the director finds time, and work bunches up in the last months before each filing deadline. A workflow tied to each client's year end turns that rolling calendar into something that runs on its own, like the other [automations for UK accounting practices](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/accountants/).

### The deadlines that start counting at each year end
Every date below is measured from the end of the company's accounting period, so each client has their own set. The figures are from gov.uk (Companies House "Late filing penalties" and HMRC "Company Tax Returns" and "Pay your Corporation Tax bill", checked November 2026). The last column is a worked example for a company with a 31 March 2026 year end.
What | Deadline | Year end 31 March 2026
--- | --- | ---
Corporation Tax payment (taxable profits up to £1.5 million) | 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period | 1 January 2027
Accounts to Companies House (private company or LLP, not its first accounts) | 9 months after the end of the accounting reference period | 31 December 2026
Company Tax Return (CT600) to HMRC | 12 months after the end of the accounting period | 31 March 2027

### What filing late costs
- Companies House charges a private company £150 if accounts are up to 1 month late, £375 up to 3 months, £750 up to 6 months and £1,500 after that. The penalty doubles if accounts are late 2 years in a row.
- HMRC charges £200 the day after a late Company Tax Return, another £200 at 3 months, then 10% of the unpaid tax at 6 months and another 10% at 12 months. If the return is late 3 times in a row, the £200 penalties become £1,000 each.
- Companies House is clear that the director is personally responsible for delivering the accounts on time, and that not filing is a criminal offence.

### Why year-end records arrive late
- Year ends are spread across the calendar, so requests depend on someone checking dates every month
- Directors get one long checklist and put it off, rather than a short list of what's actually missing
- Bank statements, loan statements, stock figures and director's loan details arrive in different places
- There's no single view of which clients are complete, partial or silent

### A rolling year-end schedule you can copy
1. Day 1 after the year end: the director gets [their own request list](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/document-chasing-email-templates/), based on last year's file, with one upload link.
2. Every 2 weeks: a reminder that names only the items still missing. It stops as soon as the file is complete.
3. Month 3: anyone still missing records moves to a firmer reminder that mentions your internal cut-off date.
4. Month 4: clients still incomplete land on your weekly call list with a summary of what's outstanding.
5. Month 6: a warning to you for any file still open, leaving 3 months before the Companies House deadline to prepare, approve and file.

### What an automated year-end workflow does
- Reads each client's year end from your client list and starts the request automatically once the year closes
- Sends each director their own list: bank and loan statements, sales and purchase records, stock, fixed asset purchases, director's loan movements
- Skips anything already coming through a bank feed, so directors are only asked for what you can't see
- Saves files with clear names in the right year-end folder and ticks them off
- Sends you one weekly list across all year ends: complete, partial and silent

### A first request you can copy
Year-end request email to a director:
```
Subject: [Company name] year end [date]: what we need from you

Hi [first name],

[Company name]'s financial year ended on [year-end date]. To prepare the accounts and Company Tax Return, please send us:

1. Bank statements for every business account up to [year-end date]
2. Loan or finance statements showing the balance on [year-end date]
3. Your stock figure on [year-end date], if you hold stock
4. Invoices for any equipment or vehicles bought in the year
5. Any money you paid into or took out of the company personally

Upload everything here: [upload link]

If we have it all by [your cut-off date], we can file comfortably before the Companies House deadline of [filing deadline].

Thanks,
[your name]
[practice name]
```

A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you request year-end records today, where your year ends are recorded and where files stall. Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/) and a clear definition of "working", for example: every client's request goes out on the day after their year end, and you see every open file on one list. It's built on the tools your practice already uses (Xero or QuickBooks, your practice management software, your email and shared drive), so nobody learns a new system. It's live in 2-3 days, and you pay once it does what we agreed and you're happy with it.

### What stays with you
The accounts, the tax and every judgement call. The workflow requests, reminds and files. You decide what counts as complete and when a director gets a phone call, and anything written to a client in your name follows wording you've approved.

### Does it work if clients use Xero with bank feeds?
Yes. Where transactions already come in through the feed, the workflow skips asking for statements and requests only what's missing, such as loan balances or stock.

### What about a client's first accounts after incorporation?
First accounts have a different deadline. Companies House says a private company's first accounts covering more than 12 months are due 21 months after incorporation, or 3 months from the accounting reference date if that is later. You enter the right date for those clients and the schedule counts from it.

## Missed call text back for contractors, and what comes after the text
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/missed-call-text-back-contractors/

Missed call text back for contractors is an automatic text sent to anyone whose call you didn't answer, usually within a minute, so they hear from you before they call the next company. A useful setup also asks what the job is and where, logs the lead in one list and offers an estimate time. In the US, business texts on a regular 10-digit number need A2P 10DLC registration first.

Missed call text back for contractors solves a simple problem: when you're on a ladder or under a sink, you can't answer the phone, and the caller moves on. A quick text keeps them with you. The text is the easy part. What matters is what happens after it: who logs the lead, who asks about the job, and who makes sure it turns into [a booked estimate](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/contractors/). This page is written for US contractors; the texting rules below are US rules.

### When a simple text-back tool is enough
If you mostly need an instant "Sorry we missed you, how can we help?" text, a standalone text-back feature from your phone provider or a low-cost app may be all you need. Try that first. A full workflow makes sense when the text is only the start, and leads still slip after the reply comes in: nobody writes them down, nobody books the visit, nobody checks back.

### What a full missed-call workflow does
- Texts the caller within a minute, from your business number, with wording you approved
- Asks a few short questions about the job: what it is, the address and how soon
- Logs every missed call and reply in [one lead list](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reply-to-new-enquiries-fast/), so nothing lives in someone's phone
- Offers estimate times from your calendar, or flags the lead for you to call back
- Follows up once if the caller goes quiet, and stops when they book, say no or reply STOP
- Skips texting numbers that are already customers with an open job, and tells you instead

### Missed call texts you can copy
Three messages (edit the wording; you approve each one before it goes live):
```
1. Within a minute of the missed call:
Hi, it's [Business]. Sorry we missed your call, we're on a job. What do you need help with, and what's the address? Reply STOP to opt out.

2. After they reply:
Thanks. You can pick a time for us to come and look here: [booking link]. If it's urgent, reply URGENT and [Your name] will call you back as soon as possible.

3. If there's no reply after 3 hours:
Just checking in from [Business]. If you still need help with the job, reply here and we'll get you booked in.
```

### Before you turn on business texting: A2P 10DLC
Texts sent from a business system to US phones on a regular 10-digit (10DLC) number have to be registered. Twilio's documentation says anyone sending SMS from an application to the US over a 10DLC number must register for A2P 10DLC, and that unregistered traffic gets extra carrier fees. The Campaign Registry, which runs the registry, describes 10DLC as a channel where brands are verified before they're allowed to send. Registration has two parts:
1. Register your brand: your legal business name, EIN (sole proprietors without one have a separate route) and contact details.
2. Register a campaign: a description of what the texts are for, and how customers opt in, opt out (STOP) and get help.
3. Wait for approval, then link your business number to the campaign. Until then, the same follow-up can run by email.

### What registration costs
Fees are set by the registry and carriers and passed on by your texting provider. These are Twilio's published A2P 10DLC fees, checked in November 2026. Other providers set their own prices, so check your provider's fee page. Toll-free numbers and short codes aren't part of 10DLC and have their own verification.
Fee (Twilio, Nov 2026) | Amount | How often
--- | --- | ---
Brand registration, sole proprietor or low-volume standard | $4.50 | One time
Brand registration, standard (includes secondary vetting) | $46 | One time
Campaign vetting | $15 | Per campaign
Campaign fee, low-volume mixed / standard | $1.50 / $10 | Monthly
Carrier fees | Set by each carrier | Per message

### How Mike Automations builds it
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how calls come in today and where leads drop off. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every missed call gets a text within a minute and lands in the lead list". It's built on what you already use (your business phone line, calendar, Google Sheets or your field service software), so there's nothing new to learn. I set up the 10DLC registration with you. It goes live in 2-3 days, costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Will the texts sound like a robot?
The wording is yours. You approve every message before it goes live. If AI drafts a reply to a customer, a person always approves it first.

### Do I need a new phone number?
Usually not. On the call we check what your current phone provider supports, and what's the simplest way to connect it. If your provider can't text from your number, we look at the options with you before anything is bought.

### How long does 10DLC registration take?
It depends on the registry and the carriers, not on me, so I won't promise a date. The workflow can go live on email first and switch to text once the campaign is approved.

### Does it work with my field service software?
It connects to the tools you already have where they allow it, so leads can go straight into your job list. Once an estimate is sent, the estimate follow-up workflow can take over.

## Subcontractor COI tracking for general contractors, without the spreadsheet
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/subcontractor-coi-tracking/

Subcontractor COI tracking means collecting a current certificate of insurance from every sub, logging each policy's expiration date and asking for the renewed certificate before it lapses. A simple workflow on your own email, drive and spreadsheet can request certificates, remind subs 60, 30 and 7 days before expiration, and give you a weekly list of who is current, expiring or missing.

Subcontractor COI tracking sounds simple: every sub on your jobs should have a current certificate of insurance on file. In practice the COIs sit in an inbox, the expiration dates live in a spreadsheet nobody updates, and you find out a policy lapsed when someone asks for it. Collecting, logging and chasing certificates is the same routine every time, so it can run on its own while you keep the decisions, the same way a [change order approval workflow](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/change-order-approval-workflow/) does.

### Why COI tracking slips
- Certificates arrive as email attachments and phone photos, and get saved in different places
- Expiration dates are typed into a spreadsheet by hand, and a spreadsheet doesn't send reminders
- Reminders, when they happen, are set from the date a COI arrived instead of the date it expires
- Nobody has one list of which subs are current, which expire soon and which are missing a certificate
- Renewals get chased the week a sub is due on site, when there's no time left

### What to check on every certificate
Most agents send the ACORD 25, the standard US certificate of liability insurance. The 2016/03 edition of the form says at the top that it is issued as a matter of information only and does not amend, extend or alter the coverage of the policies listed. It also says that if you are meant to be an additional insured, the policy must have additional insured provisions or be endorsed, and that a statement on the certificate doesn't replace the endorsement. So when your subcontract requires additional insured status or a waiver of subrogation, ask for the endorsement as well as the certificate. On each COI, check:
- The named insured matches the business name on your subcontract
- Your company is shown as the certificate holder
- Every policy your contract asks for is listed (for example general liability, auto, workers' comp, umbrella), each with a policy number and effective and expiration dates
- The limits shown meet the limits in your contract
- The additional insured and waiver of subrogation boxes, plus the endorsement itself where your contract needs it
- The producer's name and email: the agent you ask for the renewed certificate

### A COI expiration tracker you can copy
Keep one row per policy, not per sub, because a sub's general liability and workers' comp rarely expire on the same day. Sort by expiration date and the list tells you who to chase next. For illustration, as it might look on December 5:
Subcontractor | Policy | Expires | Status | Next action
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Drywall sub | General liability | Jan 4 | Expiring in 30 days | Second reminder sent, renewal requested from agent
Drywall sub | Workers' comp | Aug 15 | Current | None until June 16
Electrical sub | General liability | Dec 12 | Expiring in 7 days | Call the sub today
Plumbing sub | Auto | Not received | Missing | Request sent, not yet on site
Roofing sub | Umbrella | Nov 30 | Expired | Hold from site until a new COI is in

### What an automated COI tracking workflow does
1. When you add a new sub, it emails them a request for their COI and, if you collect it, [their W-9](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/w9-request-email-template/), with one upload link. The IRS describes Form W-9 as the form a payee uses to give their correct taxpayer identification number to the business that has to file an information return.
2. It saves every certificate in the sub's folder and logs each policy's expiration date in your tracker. AI can read the dates from a standard certificate; a person confirms them before they're used.
3. It emails the sub, and their agent if you have the address, for a renewed certificate on a schedule you choose, for example 60, 30 and 7 days before expiration.
4. It stops reminding as soon as a new certificate comes in and the new dates are confirmed.
5. It sends you a weekly list: who's current, who expires in the next 30 days, who has lapsed and who still owes you a certificate.

### A renewal request you can copy
Email to a sub 30 days before expiration:
```
Subject: Updated certificate of insurance needed by [expiration date]

Hi [first name],

Our records show your [policy type] policy expires on [expiration date]. To keep you cleared for work on our jobs, please send an updated certificate of insurance before then.

You can upload it here: [upload link]

If it's easier, forward this email to your insurance agent and ask them to send the certificate to us directly. Please list [your company name] as certificate holder and include the additional insured endorsement if your subcontract requires it.

Thanks,
[your name]
```

### When dedicated COI software makes more sense
If you manage hundreds of subs across many projects and need coverage limits checked against each contract automatically, dedicated COI tracking software may fit better. A workflow built on your own tools suits a smaller contractor who mostly needs every certificate collected, every date tracked and every renewal chased on time.

### What stays with you
You or your insurance agent decide whether the coverage meets your contract. You decide what happens when a sub's policy lapses: a phone call, a hold on site, or holding payment if your subcontract allows it. If AI drafts a reminder or reads a date from a certificate, a person always checks it before it's used.

### How it works
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you collect COIs today and where it breaks. Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/) and a clear definition of "working". It's built on what you already use (your email, Google Drive or Dropbox, Google Sheets or your project management software), so there's nothing new to learn. Live in 2-3 days. You pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Is a certificate of insurance proof that we're an additional insured?
Not on its own. The ACORD 25 says a statement on the certificate doesn't give the holder rights in place of an endorsement, so ask for the additional insured endorsement where your contract requires one.

### Can it read the expiration dates from the certificate?
AI can pull the dates from a standard certificate and fill in the tracker for you. A person always confirms them before they're used for reminders.

### Will my subs need to create an account?
No. They get an email with an upload link that works on a phone or a computer.
