## A maintenance request workflow for UK letting agents
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/letting-agent-maintenance-requests/

A maintenance request workflow for a letting agent takes every repair report through the same steps: the tenant reports it with photos on one form, urgent jobs go straight to a person, the landlord approves the rest within their agreed limit, the contractor gets the full details and the tenant is updated at each step. Nothing waits in an inbox without someone knowing.

A letting agent maintenance request workflow starts from a familiar mess. A dripping tap turns into a dozen emails: the tenant reports it, you ask for a photo, you [ask the landlord](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/landlord-repair-approval-limits/), you chase a quote, you book a contractor, and the tenant asks for an update twice along the way. Most of those steps are the same every time, which is why they can run as a workflow while you keep the decisions.

### Where repair requests get stuck
- Reports arrive by [phone, email and text](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reply-to-new-enquiries-fast/), often without a photo, an address or access details
- The landlord's approval sits in someone's inbox while the tenant waits
- Contractors get the job without the photos and access notes, so they ring the office
- Tenants chase for updates because nobody tells them what's happening
- There's no single list of open jobs, who's waiting on whom and for how long

### The rules behind repair timescales
For most tenancies of under seven years in England, section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 makes the landlord responsible for keeping the structure and exterior in repair, and the installations for water, gas, electricity, sanitation, space heating and hot water in repair and proper working order. The same section lets the landlord enter to view the condition of the property at reasonable times on 24 hours' notice in writing to the occupier. Awaab's Law has applied to social landlords in England since 27 October 2025: gov.uk says they must fix emergency health and safety hazards within 24 hours of them being reported. The government has said it will extend Awaab's Law to private renting through the Renters' Rights Act, so check gov.uk for when, and on what timescales, it applies to the homes you manage. Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own rules.

### A maintenance triage table you can adapt
Agree categories and response targets with your landlords and write them into your terms of business. The targets below are an example to start from, not legal deadlines. For illustration:
Priority | Examples | Who handles it | Example target
--- | --- | --- | ---
Emergency | Gas smell, no heating or hot water in winter, major leak, unsafe electrics, can't secure the property | A person, straight away, by phone. For a gas smell, the tenant calls the gas emergency line first | Contractor attending the same day
Urgent | Boiler fault with some heating, blocked only toilet, broken window lock, fridge or oven failure in a furnished let | Flagged to a person, landlord told immediately | Contractor booked within 1-3 working days
Routine | Dripping tap, sticking door, broken extractor fan, cracked tile | Workflow: landlord approval, then contractor | Contractor booked within 10 working days
Planned | Redecoration, replacing worn carpets, garden work | Added to the landlord's planned works list | Agreed with the landlord

### What an automated maintenance workflow does
1. The tenant reports the repair on one simple form, with photos, a description and access times. The form asks the triage questions first, and anything that sounds like an emergency shows the right phone number straight away.
2. Every request is logged against the property in one list, with a status anyone in the office can see.
3. Emergency and urgent jobs go to a person in the office or on call, never into a queue.
4. For routine jobs, the landlord gets the details and photos and an approve button. Jobs under the spending limit they've agreed with you can go ahead without waiting.
5. The approved contractor gets the job details, photos and access notes, and is asked to confirm a date.
6. The tenant is updated at each step, and you get a daily list of jobs that have waited longer than your targets.

### A tenant update you can copy
Message to the tenant once a contractor is booked:
```
Hi [tenant name],

Thanks for reporting the [repair] at [address]. Your landlord has approved the work and [contractor name] will visit on [date] between [time window].

They'll need access to [room]. If that time doesn't suit, reply to this message by [date] and we'll rearrange.

If anything gets worse before then, call us on [office number]. For a gas smell, call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999 first.

[your name], [agency name]
```

### What stays with you
Anything urgent or safety related goes straight to a person, never into a queue. You decide which contractor to use, what counts as urgent and when to step in. If AI drafts a message to a tenant or landlord, a person always approves it before it's sent.

### How it works
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how repairs are reported today and where they stall. Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/) and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools your agency already uses (your email, your property management software where it allows a connection, and a shared spreadsheet or drive), so nobody learns a new system. Live in 2-3 days. You pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Do tenants need to download an app?
No. They use a link to a simple form that works on a phone or a computer.

### We already use property management software. Does this replace it?
No. It connects to what you have where the software allows it, and fills the gaps, such as chasing approvals and keeping tenants updated.

### What about emergencies?
You decide what counts as an emergency. Those requests skip the queue and go straight to a person in the office or on call, and the form shows the tenant the right number to ring.

### Can landlords pre-approve small repairs?
Yes. If a landlord agrees a spending limit with you, jobs under it go straight to the contractor and the landlord is told afterwards.

### How much does it cost?
Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000, paid once it's running and you're happy with it. The first 3 businesses pay $1,500. Optional support is $150 a month.

## Law firm client intake automation for solicitors
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/law-firm-client-intake/

Law firm client intake automation runs the repeatable steps between a new enquiry and a signed client care letter: an instant reply with a short form, a conflict check before any consultation is booked, the engagement letter, and the ID and documents you need. A person makes every legal decision, including whether there is a conflict and whether to take the matter on.

Law firm client intake automation starts the moment [a new enquiry](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reply-to-new-enquiries-fast/) comes in, because the same steps follow every time: call back, ask the same questions, check for conflicts, book a consultation, send the client care letter, chase the signature and the ID documents. When that runs from memory, enquiries wait and some go elsewhere. Intake is a process, and most of it can run on its own while your solicitors keep every decision. This page is written for small firms in England and Wales regulated by the SRA. Once a matter is open, [progress updates for conveyancing clients](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/conveyancing-client-progress-updates/) can run the same way.

### Where intake slows down
- Enquiries come in by phone, email and web form, and each gets written up by hand
- Basic details, including the other parties, are asked for again on the first call
- The conflict check depends on someone remembering to run it before the consultation is booked
- Client care letters go out late, and signatures and ID documents need chasing
- Nobody has one list of enquiries, where each one stands and who is following up

### The rules intake has to respect
The SRA Code of Conduct for Solicitors sets several things that sit inside intake. Paragraph 8.1 says you identify who you are acting for. Paragraph 6.2 says you do not act where there is a conflict of interest, apart from narrow exceptions, so the check has to happen before advice is given. Paragraph 8.3 says clients are told in writing at the time of engagement about their right to complain, and paragraph 8.7 says they get the best possible information about how their matter will be priced. For work in scope of the Money Laundering Regulations 2017, which the SRA's scope guidance says includes [property conveyancing](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/conveyancing-source-of-funds-document-chasing/) and buying or selling a business, you also need client due diligence and a risk assessment on the matter. A workflow can make sure each step happens in order and is recorded. It cannot decide any of them for you.

### The intake checklist the workflow follows
Step | What the workflow does | Who decides
--- | --- | ---
1. Enquiry received | Replies within minutes with a short form: name, contact details, matter type, other parties, key dates | Nobody: automatic
2. Enquiry logged | Adds it to one list with its source and status | Nobody: automatic
3. Conflict check | Sends the client and other party names to whoever runs your check | A person clears or declines
4. Consultation | Offers booking times only after the check is cleared | Fee earner
5. Take on the matter | Asks the fee earner to confirm yes or no, and sends a polite decline if no | Fee earner
6. Client care letter | Sends your letter, with costs and complaints information, for e-signature | Fee earner approves the content
7. ID and due diligence | Requests ID and, for in-scope matters, the documents your AML policy needs | Your compliance person reviews
8. Follow-up | Reminds about anything unsigned or missing, then tells a person | Nobody until it escalates
9. Open the file | Once everything is in, opens the matter in your practice software where it allows a connection | Fee earner confirms

### First reply you can copy
Automatic reply to a new enquiry:
```
Subject: Your enquiry to [firm name]

Dear [first name],

Thank you for contacting [firm name] about [matter type]. We've received your enquiry.

Before we can discuss your matter, we need to check that we are free to act for you. Please fill in this short form with your details and the names of anyone else involved: [form link]. It takes about three minutes.

Once we've completed our checks, we'll send you a link to book a consultation. Please don't send any documents yet.

Kind regards,
[name]
[firm name]
```

### Why speed matters
People who need a solicitor often contact more than one firm. A reply within minutes keeps the enquiry warm while the conflict check runs, and it tells the client what happens next instead of leaving them to wonder. The general approach for any business is in our guide to replying to new enquiries fast.

### What stays with you
Every legal judgement. A person decides whether a conflict exists, whether to take the matter, what goes into the client care letter and whether the due diligence is enough. The workflow collects, reminds and files. If AI drafts a reply to a prospective client, a person always approves it before it goes out.

### How Mike Automations would build it
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how enquiries come in today and where they wait. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools your firm already uses (your email, calendar, e-signature tool and practice management software where it allows a connection), so nobody learns a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Does the workflow run the conflict check?
It gathers the names and passes them to the person who checks them, in your practice software or your own records. A person always decides whether there's a conflict.

### Can it work with our practice management software?
It connects to the tools you already have where they allow it. On the call we check exactly what can be connected in your setup, and what's better left manual.

### Does it handle AML checks?
It requests and collects the ID and documents your AML policy asks for, and tracks what's missing. Your compliance person reviews them and decides. If you already use an ID verification service, the workflow can send the client its link.

### What about client confidentiality?
The data stays in your accounts: your email, your drive, your software. I only get the access the workflow needs, and the data is never used for anything else.

### How much does it cost?
Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000, paid once it's running and you're happy with it. The first 3 businesses pay $1,500. Optional support is $150 a month.

## Gas safety, EICR and EPC reminders for letting agents
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/letting-agent-compliance-certificate-reminders/

Gas safety, EICR and EPC reminders for letting agents work best as one list of every property and certificate, with renewals started weeks before each expiry date. In England a gas safety check is due every 12 months, an electrical inspection (EICR) at least every 5 years, and an EPC lasts 10 years. A workflow can book the renewal, collect the new certificate and flag anything late, while a person checks each document.

Gas safety, EICR and EPC reminders are the dates a letting agent cannot afford to miss, and every managed property has its own set. Most agencies track them in a spreadsheet that one person keeps up to date. Chasing renewals is the same steps every time, so it can run as a workflow while your team keeps the checks. [Right to rent follow-up checks](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/right-to-rent-follow-up-check-reminders/) work the same way. This page covers the rules for private lettings in England; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own rules, so check those for properties there.

### The renewal dates in England
These are the main certificates for a private let in England, from the official guidance as it stood in November 2026. HSE says gas safety checks must be done every year by a Gas Safe registered engineer, and the record kept for 2 years. Since 2018 the check can be done up to 2 months before the due date while keeping the original deadline, so booking early does not shorten the cycle. The Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 (regulation 3, on legislation.gov.uk) require an inspection at least every 5 years, or sooner if the last report says so. Gov.uk says an EPC is valid for 10 years and must be ordered before you market a property to let.
Certificate | How often | Copy to tenants | When to start the renewal (suggested)
--- | --- | --- | ---
Gas safety record | Every 12 months (HSE) | Existing tenants within 28 days of the check; new tenants before they move in | 8 weeks before expiry: a check in the last 2 months keeps the original date
EICR (electrical report) | At least every 5 years, or sooner if the report says so | Existing tenants within 28 days; new tenants before they move in; a prospective tenant within 28 days of a written request | 3 months before expiry, to allow time for any remedial work
EICR remedial work | Within 28 days of the inspection, or sooner if the report says so | Written confirmation to tenants and the council within 28 days of the work being done | Same day the report arrives
EPC | Valid for 10 years | Shown to anyone renting the property | Before marketing a re-let if the EPC has expired

### Where certificate tracking breaks down
- Expiry dates live in a spreadsheet, a calendar and people's heads, and they don't always agree
- Renewals get booked late because nobody saw the date coming
- The engineer does the check, but the new certificate never makes it into the property file
- The tenant never gets their copy within the 28 days, because nobody was asked to send it
- An EICR comes back unsatisfactory and [the 28-day clock for remedial work](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/eicr-remedial-work-follow-up-electricians/) starts without anyone noticing

### What an automated reminder workflow does
1. Keeps one list of every property, each certificate it needs and its expiry date, in the spreadsheet or software you already use.
2. Sends you a weekly list of anything missing, expired or due in the next 90 days.
3. Contacts your usual engineer or the landlord at the lead time you set, with the address and access details, and asks for a date.
4. After the visit, asks for the new certificate, files it against the property and puts it in front of a person to check.
5. Once a person has checked it, updates the expiry date and sends the tenant their copy, logging the date it went out.
6. If an EICR lists remedial work, starts a 28-day tracker for that property and chases the contractor for written confirmation.
7. Tells a named person when a date is close and nothing has been booked.

### A reminder you can copy
Email to a landlord who arranges their own gas safety check:
```
Subject: Gas safety record due for [property address] on [expiry date]

Hi [landlord name],

The gas safety record for [property address] expires on [expiry date]. A check can be done up to 2 months early without changing the renewal date, so now is a good time to book it.

Once your Gas Safe engineer has visited, please upload the new record here: [upload link]. We'll check it, send the tenant their copy and update our records.

If you'd like us to arrange the check with our usual engineer instead, just reply to this email.

Thanks,
[your name]
[agency name]
```

### What stays with you
The legal duties stay with the landlord and with you as their agent, and the workflow doesn't change that. You choose which certificates each property needs and how early to start. A person checks each new certificate before the date in the list is updated, and decides what happens when a check fails, a report is unsatisfactory or a date is missed. If AI reads a date from a certificate or drafts a message to a landlord, a person always approves it first.

Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools your agency already uses (your email, a shared spreadsheet or drive, and your property management software where it allows a connection), so nobody learns a new system. ### We already have property management software. Does this replace it?
No. Many systems store the dates. This adds the chasing around them: booking the renewal, collecting the certificate, sending the tenant's copy and telling you what's still open.

You set which certificates each property needs and how early to start the renewal. On the call we go through your list, including any properties in Scotland or Wales, where the rules differ. The workflow follows your settings, it doesn't give legal advice.

## A change order approval workflow for contractors
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/change-order-approval-workflow/

A change order approval workflow gets every change on a job written down, priced and signed by the customer or GC before the extra work starts. The crew logs the change on a phone, the office prices it from your template, it goes out for e-signature with automatic reminders, and the crew lead is told the moment it's approved.

A change order approval workflow fixes a familiar problem for [contractors](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/contractors/). The homeowner asks for an extra outlet, the GC wants a different finish, or you open a wall and find rot. The crew is ready to keep going, the change is agreed by phone and the paperwork comes later, if at all. Then the invoice turns into an argument. Getting a written, signed approval before the extra work starts is the same few steps every time, so it can run as a workflow while you keep the pricing and the decisions.

### Where change orders go wrong
- Changes are agreed verbally on site and never written down
- The office hears about the change after the work is done
- Change orders go out by email and sit unsigned while the job moves on
- Nobody can quickly say which changes on a job are approved, pending or rejected
- Approved changes don't make it onto the final invoice

### Why the signature has to come first
Beyond avoiding arguments, some states set rules for this. In California, Business and Professions Code section 7159 says a home improvement contract must tell the buyer that extra work or a change order is not enforceable against them unless it states in writing, before the work starts, the scope of the work, the amount added to or taken off the contract, and the effect on progress payments or the completion date. Rules differ by state and by type of work, so check yours with your attorney or your state licensing board. On signing, the federal ESIGN Act (15 U.S.C. 7001) says a signature or contract may not be denied legal effect solely because it is in electronic form, which is why an e-signature on a phone can do the job of a paper signature on most change orders.

### What every change order should include
Use your own template and terms. These are the fields that stop most disputes, including the three the California rule names:
Field | What to write
--- | ---
Job and change number | Job name or address, and CO #1, #2 and so on, so changes can't be confused
Requested by | Homeowner, GC, architect, or found on site, with the date
Scope of the change | What will be added, removed or done differently, in plain words, with photos
Price | The amount added to or taken off the contract, and the new contract total
Schedule | Days added to or taken off, and the new completion date
Payments | How the change affects the progress payment schedule
Approval | Customer or GC name, signature and date, collected before the work starts

### What an automated change order workflow does
1. Your crew lead opens a link on their phone and logs the change: what, why, photos and a rough scope. It takes a couple of minutes on site.
2. The workflow turns it into a draft change order from your own template, numbered for that job, and sends it to the office.
3. Someone in the office prices it, checks the schedule impact and approves the draft.
4. It goes to the customer or GC for e-signature. If it isn't signed within the time you set, for example by the next morning, a reminder goes out and the office is told.
5. Once it's signed, the crew lead gets a text that the work can go ahead, and the signed copy is saved in the job folder.
6. Approved changes go on the job's change log and onto the list for invoicing, so nothing is missed on the final bill.

### A message to the customer you can copy
Text or email sent with the change order:
```
Hi [customer name], this is [your name] from [company]. As we discussed on site today, here is change order #[number] for [job address]: [one-line description of the change].

It adds $[amount] to the contract and [number] days to the schedule. Please review and sign here: [e-signature link]

We'll start this part of the work as soon as it's signed. Any questions, just reply or call me on [phone].
```

### What stays with you
You price every change and decide what goes into the change order. A person in your office reviews it before it goes to the customer, and you decide what happens when a change is urgent or a customer refuses. If AI drafts the description or a message to the customer, a person always approves it before it's sent. If you work in the UK, the same process is usually called a variation; the workflow is the same, but the contract terms are different, so use your own.

### How it works
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how changes are agreed on your jobs today. Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/) and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your email, phones, e-signature tool, and your job management or accounting software where it allows a connection), so your crew doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. You pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Does my crew need to learn new software?
No. They fill in a short form from a link on their phone. Everything else happens in the office or by email.

### Can it use our own change order template?
Yes. The change order is built from your template and your terms. Pricing stays with you.

### Is an e-signature valid on a change order?
Under the federal ESIGN Act a signature can't be refused legal effect just because it's electronic. Some contracts or states add their own requirements, so check yours with your attorney.

### What if the change is urgent and work can't stop?
You decide the rule for urgent changes, for example a phone call to the office. The workflow still logs it and sends the paperwork for signature straight away.

### How much does it cost?
Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000, paid once it's running and you're happy with it. The first 3 businesses pay $1,500. Optional support is $150 a month.

## Client onboarding automation for marketing agencies
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agency-client-onboarding-automation/

Client onboarding automation for a marketing agency is a workflow that starts when a client accepts the proposal and handles the routine setup: the contract for e-signature, the first invoice, the brief form, brand files and access to analytics and ad accounts. It asks for access through each platform's own user and partner settings rather than passwords, reminds the client about anything still missing, and gives your team one checklist per client before the kickoff.

Client onboarding automation matters because the first two weeks with a new client usually go on admin. The contract, the first invoice, the brief, brand files, and access to the website, analytics and ad accounts each need their own email and their own follow-up, and work can't start until it's all in. Onboarding is the same checklist for every client, so it can run as a workflow while your team prepares the kickoff. It's often the first of the [automations for marketing agencies](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agencies/) worth setting up.

### Where agency onboarding slows down
- Access to ad accounts, analytics and the website trickles in over weeks
- Clients send passwords by email, which is risky for them and for you
- The brief questionnaire comes back half filled in
- The first invoice and the signed contract need separate chasing
- Nobody can see at a glance what's still missing for each new client

### An onboarding checklist you can copy
Change the rows to match the services you sell. Each row becomes one tracked item per client, and the client is only reminded about rows that are still open.
Item | How it's requested | Done when
--- | --- | ---
Signed contract | Sent for e-signature when the proposal is accepted | The signed copy is saved to the client folder
First invoice | Created in your invoicing tool and emailed with a payment link | Your accounting software shows it paid
Brief and key contacts | One onboarding form | Every required question is answered
Brand files | Upload link in the same form | Logo, fonts and guidelines are in the folder
Google Analytics | Short guide to adding your agency's email as a user | Your team confirms the access works
Google Ads | Short guide to inviting your agency's email | Invitation accepted
Meta ad account and pages | Short guide to adding your agency as a partner | Assets show in your business portfolio
Website | A user account with the role you need, never a shared password | Your team can log in

### How access is requested without passwords
The major ad and analytics platforms let a client give access without sharing a password. Google's help pages (checked November 2026) explain that in Google Analytics a client opens Admin, then Access Management, adds your email address and chooses a role such as Viewer, Editor or Administrator, at account or property level. In Google Ads they go to Admin, then Access and security, and invite your email with an access level. Meta's Business Help Centre covers giving a partner access to business assets in a business portfolio. The workflow sends each client a short guide for the platforms they actually use, then checks back until the access is confirmed. Menus change, so the guides are reviewed when you sign off the plan.

### What an automated onboarding workflow does
1. Starts when the proposal is accepted, and sends the contract for e-signature and the first invoice, with [automatic payment reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) if it goes unpaid.
2. Sends one onboarding form for the brief, brand files and key contacts.
3. Sends the access guides that match the services the client bought.
4. Creates the client's folder, project and channel in the tools you already use.
5. Reminds the client about anything still missing, every few days, until it's in.
6. Gives your team one checklist per client, so the kickoff call starts with everything ready, including how [client approvals](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/agency-client-approvals/) will work.

### A welcome email you can copy
Welcome email sent after the contract is signed:
```
Subject: Welcome to [agency name]: 3 things before we start

Hi [first name],

Thanks for signing, we're looking forward to working with you. To get started on [start date], we need three things from you:

1. The onboarding form (about 10 minutes): [form link]
2. Your brand files, uploaded here: [upload link]
3. Access to [Google Analytics / Google Ads / Meta]. Step-by-step guides are here: [guide link]. Please don't send passwords by email.

Your first invoice is attached and can be paid here: [payment link].

Any questions, just reply to this email.

[your name]
[agency name]
```

### What stays with you
The relationship and the strategy. Your team decides the scope, runs the kickoff and checks that the access you were given is the access you need. If AI drafts a welcome email or summarises the brief, a person always approves it before it goes out.

### How it works
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you onboard clients today and where it stalls. Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/) and a clear definition of "working", for example: every accepted proposal triggers the contract, invoice and form, and no client reaches kickoff with an open item you didn't know about. It's built on the tools your agency already uses (your email, e-signature, invoicing, project management and shared drive, where they allow a connection), so nobody learns a new system. Live in 2-3 days. You pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Do clients have to share their passwords?
No. Wherever a platform lets them add your agency as a user or partner, that's what the workflow asks for. Passwords stay with the client.

### Can it work with our project management and invoicing tools?
It connects to the tools you already use where they allow it. On the call we check exactly what can be connected in your setup, and what's better left manual.

### We onboard different services differently. Is that a problem?
No. The form and checklist can change with the service the client bought, so an SEO client and a paid ads client get the right requests.

### What if the client's ad account is owned by a previous agency?
The workflow can't fix ownership, but it can spot it: if access isn't confirmed after the reminders, the item goes to your account manager with a note to ask the client who owns the account.

## Physio patient intake forms before the first appointment
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/physio-clinic-patient-intake-forms/

Physio patient intake forms work best when they are sent automatically as soon as a new patient books, with a reminder a day or two before the appointment if the form isn't back. The answers go into the patient's record so the physio can read them before the session. Because the form holds health information, it is special category data under UK GDPR and needs extra care.

Physio patient intake forms are meant to save time, but in many small clinics they don't. A new patient books, turns up, and spends the first ten minutes of a paid session on a clipboard: medical history, medication, consent, contact details. Or the form was emailed, but nobody checked whether it came back. Getting intake done before the patient walks in is the same few steps for every booking, so it can run as a workflow while your clinicians keep every clinical decision. The same booking flow can also help [reduce no-shows](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reduce-appointment-no-shows/).

### Where intake goes wrong in a small clinic
- Forms are filled in on paper in reception and typed up later
- The emailed form link is sent once, and nobody follows up
- The physio only finds out about an answer that matters at the start of the session
- Consent forms are missing or stored somewhere separate from the patient record
- Reception can't see at a glance which of tomorrow's new patients still owe a form

### What an automated intake workflow does
1. A new patient books online or through reception, as they do today.
2. Within minutes, they get the right intake and consent form for that appointment type, by email or text.
3. If the form isn't back two days before the appointment, a short reminder goes out. A second one follows the day before.
4. Completed answers are filed to the patient's record in your clinic software, where it allows a connection.
5. Answers your clinicians have asked to see in advance are flagged to the treating physio.
6. Each morning, reception gets a list of the day's new patients whose forms are still missing.

### Intake form fields to consider
Your clinicians decide what the form asks. This list is a starting point to review, not a clinical template. Ask only for what you need for the first assessment: the less health data you collect, the less you have to protect.
Section | Typical fields | Note
--- | --- | ---
About you | Full name, date of birth, address, phone, email, preferred contact method | Used for booking and reminders
Who's paying | Self-pay or insurer, insurer name, policy and authorisation number | Only if you bill insurers
Referral | Self-referred or referred, referrer's name, GP name and practice | GP details only if you write to GPs
Your problem | Main problem, where it is, when and how it started, what makes it better or worse | Free text is fine
Your health | Medical conditions, past surgery, current medication, allergies | Health data: special category
Your goals | What you want to be able to do again | Helps plan the first session
Consent and privacy | Consent to assessment and treatment, how you'll use their data, contact preferences | Wording set by your clinic

### Health data and UK GDPR
The ICO lists data concerning health as special category data under UK GDPR (our [GDPR checklist for automating client data](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gdpr-checklist-automating-client-data/) covers the general points). ICO guidance says that to process it you need a lawful basis under Article 6 and a separate condition under Article 9; for a clinic that is often the health or social care condition in Article 9(2)(h). The ICO also says you must carry out a data protection impact assessment if you plan to process special category data on a large scale, and you must check whether you need an appropriate policy document under the Data Protection Act 2018. Your clinic decides these points, ideally with your data protection adviser. In practice the workflow keeps forms inside tools your clinic already controls, sends links rather than attachments, and only shows answers to the people who need them.

### Reminder you can copy
Text reminder two days before the first appointment:
```
Hi [first name], it's [clinic name]. Your first appointment is on [day] at [time]. Please fill in your health questionnaire before you come: [secure form link]. It takes about 5 minutes and means your physio can spend the whole session on you. Any problems, call us on [clinic phone].
```

### What stays with you
All clinical judgement. Your clinicians decide what the form asks, read the answers and decide what happens next. A form does not replace the consent conversation in the session. If AI summarises a form for a clinician, a person always reads the original before acting on it, and nothing is sent to a patient without a person approving the wording.

### How Mike Automations would build it
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how new patients are booked and onboarded today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your booking or practice management software, email and forms, where they allow a connection), so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Does it replace our practice management software?
No. It works alongside the tools you already use. Many clinic systems already send forms; on the call we check what yours does on its own, and only automate the gaps, such as the reminders and the morning list.

### What if a patient never fills in the form?
They get reminders before the appointment, and reception sees them on the morning list. They can still complete it on arrival, as they do today.

### Can different appointments get different forms?
Yes. A new sports injury assessment and a post-surgery referral can each get their own form and their own consent wording.

### Is it safe to collect health information this way?
Health information is special category data under UK GDPR, so it needs extra care. The forms stay in tools your clinic controls, only the people who need the answers see them, and your clinic keeps its own lawful basis and policies. On the call we look at where your data is stored today.

### How much does it cost?

## HVAC maintenance agreement renewals, tracked and reminded automatically
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/hvac-maintenance-agreement-renewals/

Automating HVAC maintenance agreement renewals means keeping one list of every plan and its expiration date, reminding each customer by email and text before the plan lapses, and asking them to book the tune-ups their plan covers. Customers who don't renew land on a short list for a personal call, so no agreement lapses without anyone noticing.

HVAC maintenance agreement renewals are easy to lose track of. Agreements bring in steady work and customers who call you first, but renewals are usually tracked in a spreadsheet or in someone's head, and when the season gets busy, plans quietly lapse. Remembering who expires when, reminding them and booking the visits is the same routine every month, so it can run as a workflow, just like [estimate follow-up](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/contractors/).

### Where maintenance agreements slip
- Expiration dates live in a spreadsheet that nobody checks during peak season
- Customers get one renewal email, if any, and then nothing
- Spring and fall tune-ups covered by the plan never get scheduled
- The office can't quickly see how many agreements expire next month
- Lapsed customers aren't followed up, so they drift to whoever answers first

### Why the tune-up reminders matter as much as the renewal
A plan customer who never gets a visit has little reason to renew. ENERGY STAR's maintenance checklist recommends annual pre-season check-ups by a contractor: the cooling system in the spring and the heating system in the fall, before contractors get busy. Booking those visits early fills your shoulder seasons and gives the customer a reason to keep the plan. The workflow can ask each plan customer to pick a time a few weeks before each season starts.

### A renewal reminder sequence you can copy
Adjust the timing to your plans. This works for an annual agreement paid up front:
When | Channel | What it says
--- | --- | ---
45 days before expiration | Email | Your plan renews on [date]: what's covered, the renewal price and a link to renew or pay
21 days before | Text | Short reminder with the renewal link
7 days before | Email and text | Last reminder before the plan lapses, and what the customer loses (priority service, plan discounts, covered tune-ups)
On the expiration date | Office list | Customer goes on the lapsed list for a personal call
14 days after | Email | Your plan has lapsed: a link to restart it, sent once, then no more automatic messages
Once renewed | Email or text | Thank you, and a link to book the next covered tune-up

### A renewal email you can copy
First reminder, 45 days before expiration:
```
Subject: Your [company] maintenance plan renews on [expiration date]

Hi [first name],

Your [plan name] for [address] runs until [expiration date]. It covers [number] tune-ups a year, priority scheduling and [plan benefit].

To keep your plan active, renew here: [renewal or payment link]. The renewal price is $[amount] for the next 12 months.

Once you've renewed, we'll send you a link to book your [spring/fall] tune-up.

Questions? Reply to this email or call us on [phone].

[your name], [company]
```

### What an automated renewal workflow does
1. Keeps one list of every agreement with the customer, address, plan, start date, expiration date and visits used, built from your spreadsheet or your field service software.
2. Sends the renewal reminders above by email or text, with [a link to renew or pay](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) using the payment tool you already have.
3. Marks the agreement renewed when payment comes in and stops the reminders.
4. Asks plan customers to pick a time for each covered tune-up before the season starts.
5. Gives the office a weekly list of agreements expiring in the next 60 days, tune-ups still to book, and plans that have lapsed.

### If your agreements renew automatically
Auto-renewing plans come with extra rules in some states. In California, for example, Business and Professions Code section 17602 requires a business to send an annual reminder to a consumer on an annual automatic renewal agreement, stating the service, how often and how much they're charged, and how to cancel. Other states have their own auto-renewal laws, so check your state's rules with your attorney before you set the reminders. The workflow can send whatever notices you decide on, on time, and keep a record that they went out.

### What stays with you
Your plans, your prices and your terms. You decide what each agreement covers, when reminders go out and how to handle a customer who wants to cancel. If AI drafts a reminder or a reply, a person always approves it before it's sent.

### How it works
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you sell and track maintenance agreements today. Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/) and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your field service software, spreadsheet, email, texting and payment tools, where they allow a connection), so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. You pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### We track agreements in a spreadsheet. Is that enough?
Yes. The workflow can start from the spreadsheet you have, or from your field service software if it allows a connection.

### Can customers renew without calling the office?
Yes, if you take payments online. The reminder includes a link to pay, and the agreement is marked renewed once payment comes in.

### Does it work for plumbing or electrical service plans too?
Yes. Any service plan with a start date, an expiration date and scheduled visits works the same way.

### Can it send the annual notice our state requires for auto-renewing plans?
It can send the notice you and your attorney decide on, to every customer, on time, and log when it went out. The wording and the rules are yours to confirm.

## Conveyancing client updates without the chasing calls
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/conveyancing-client-progress-updates/

Conveyancing client updates are short messages sent to a buyer or seller each time their file reaches a milestone, such as searches ordered, mortgage offer received or exchange. Sent automatically when the fee earner records the milestone, they tell the client what has happened, what comes next and whether anything is needed from them, which cuts the number of "any update?" calls.

Conveyancing client updates are the answer to the question every buyer and seller asks: where does my move stand? Without them, clients phone, and so do their estate agents and brokers. Each call pulls a fee earner away from the file, and most ask the same thing: has anything happened yet? Telling clients what has happened at each milestone is the same message every time, so it can go out as a workflow while your fee earners keep the legal work. It picks up where [client intake](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/law-firm-client-intake/) leaves off.

### Why progress calls pile up
- Clients only hear from the firm when something is needed from them
- Long waits, such as for searches or the other side's replies to enquiries, look like nothing is happening
- Estate agents and brokers call separately for the same update
- Updates depend on a busy fee earner remembering to send them
- Clients don't know what the next step is or what they need to do

### What an automated update workflow does
1. The fee earner records a milestone on the file, as they do today, in your case management system or a shared tracker.
2. The workflow picks the matching message, written and approved by your firm in advance, and fills in the client's name and property.
3. It sends the update by email or text, whichever the client chose at the start, when the [source of funds documents](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/conveyancing-source-of-funds-document-chasing/) were requested.
4. If the client has agreed, the estate agent gets a shorter matching update.
5. When the message asks the client for something, a reminder follows if it doesn't arrive.
6. Each week the team gets a list of files where nothing has been recorded for a set number of days, for a personal check-in.

### A purchase update sequence you can adapt
These are the milestones most purchase files go through in England and Wales. Your firm will have its own wording and may track more or fewer steps. Keep each message short and plain, and never put advice in an automatic update.
Milestone recorded | What the client is told | Anything needed from them?
--- | --- | ---
File opened | Who their fee earner is, how updates will arrive, and roughly what the stages are | ID and source of funds documents, if not already sent
Contract pack received | The seller's solicitor has sent the draft contract and property information, and it is being reviewed | No
Searches ordered | What searches are and that results can take a while to come back | No
Mortgage offer received | The lender has issued the offer and the firm is checking its conditions | No, unless the firm asks
Enquiries raised | Questions have gone to the seller's solicitor; waiting for replies is normal | No
Report on title sent | Their report is ready to read, with a request to get in touch with any questions | Read the report and sign the documents
Ready to exchange | Everything is in place, and the fee earner will call to agree the completion date | Deposit funds, if not already sent
Exchanged | Contracts have exchanged and the purchase is now legally binding, with the completion date | No
Completed | Keys can be collected, and what happens next with Stamp Duty and registration | No

### Message you can copy
Update when searches are ordered:
```
Subject: Your purchase of [property address]: searches ordered

Dear [client name],

A quick update: today we ordered the property searches for [property address]. These check things like local planning, drainage and environmental records.

Results usually take a while to come back, and the timing depends on the local council and the other search providers. You don't need to do anything at the moment. We'll write again as soon as the results are in.

If you have a question in the meantime, reply to this email and [fee earner name] will get back to you.

Kind regards,
[firm name]
```

### After completion
Updates don't stop at completion. Gov.uk says a Stamp Duty Land Tax return must be sent and any tax paid within 14 days of completion, and that a solicitor or agent usually does this for the buyer. SDLT applies in England and Northern Ireland; Scotland has Land and Buildings Transaction Tax and Wales has Land Transaction Tax. A short message confirming the return has been filed, and a later one when registration at HM Land Registry is complete, closes the file cleanly and saves another round of calls.

### What stays with you
All legal advice and every judgement on the file. The workflow sends pre-approved messages about milestones your team records; it never advises. Anything unusual, such as a problem with the title or a chain issue, is handled by the fee earner personally. If AI drafts an update, a person always approves it before it's sent.

## WhatsApp quote follow-up for tradespeople: what to send and when
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/whatsapp-quote-follow-up-tradespeople/

WhatsApp quote follow-up for tradespeople works best as three short messages: a check that the quote arrived and made sense, a useful nudge about five days later, and a polite message about a week after that which closes the quote, then you stop. If the messages go out automatically through the WhatsApp Business Platform, Meta only allows approved templates once 24 hours have passed since the customer last wrote, and the customer must have agreed to hear from your business by name.

WhatsApp quote follow-up for tradespeople is the job most UK trades never get round to. You price a rewire, a bathroom or a boiler swap, send it on WhatsApp, see the two blue ticks, and then hear nothing. Chasing feels pushy, so it doesn't happen, and the job goes to whoever asked again. This page gives you a three-message sequence with timing, explains how [WhatsApp Business templates and opt-in](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/text-or-whatsapp-clients-for-documents/) work under Meta's own rules, and splits what can run on its own from what should stay with you.

### Why customers go quiet after a quote
Only the last one is a lost job. The others are a reply that never got written, and a short, friendly message usually brings it out. A clear "no" is useful too: you can stop holding the date and stop thinking about it.
- They're waiting on other quotes and haven't decided yet
- They read it on the bus, meant to reply, and it slid down the chat list
- A line in the quote confused them (what's included, VAT, the start date) and they didn't want to ask
- The price was higher than they hoped, and silence feels easier than saying so
- They've picked someone else and don't want the awkward conversation

### A 3-message WhatsApp follow-up sequence
This timing is a starting point, not a rule. Shorten it for urgent work like a leak or a failed boiler, and stretch it for a kitchen or an extension that the customer will plan for weeks. Every message stops the moment the customer replies.
Message | When | What it does
--- | --- | ---
1. Check it arrived | 1 to 2 days after the quote | Confirms they got it and invites questions, so a confusing line gets asked about
2. Useful nudge | About 5 days after the quote | Gives one real reason to decide: your next free dates, or an answer to a common question
3. Close the quote | About 12 days after the quote | Says you'll take it as a no for now, with no hard feelings, and leaves the door open
Stop | After message 3 | No more automatic messages. If they come back later, you pick it up yourself

### The three messages, ready to copy
WhatsApp quote follow-up messages (edit the words in brackets):
```
Message 1
Hi [first name], it's [your name] from [business]. Just checking the quote for [job] came through OK. If anything in it isn't clear, ask away and I'll explain.

Message 2
Hi [first name], [your name] from [business] again. I've got space to start [job] on [date] or [date] if that suits. Happy to answer any questions about the quote first.

Message 3 (close the quote)
Hi [first name], I haven't heard back about [job], so I'll assume it's on hold or you've gone another way, no problem at all. If you want to pick it up later, just reply here and I'll check the price still stands. Thanks for asking me to quote.
```

### How WhatsApp Business templates and opt-in work
If you send these yourself from the free WhatsApp Business app, you're simply [replying to a customer who contacted you](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reply-to-new-enquiries-fast/). The app's own tools help (saved quick replies, greeting and away messages), but you still press send. To send a timed sequence automatically, the messages go through the WhatsApp Business Platform (Meta's Cloud API), usually via a provider, and Meta's developer documentation sets the rules:
- When a customer messages you, a 24-hour customer service window opens, and each new message from them resets it. Inside the window you can send normal messages
- Outside that window you can only send message templates that Meta has reviewed and approved. Meta says review can take up to 24 hours. Templates use placeholders such as {{1}} for the customer's name and the job
- Every template has a category: utility, marketing or authentication. Meta describes utility templates as non-promotional and tied to something the customer asked for. Add a discount or an offer and it becomes marketing, which Meta prices differently
- Opt-in: Meta requires that the customer clearly agreed to receive messages from your business, with your business name stated. A line on your quote such as "We'll follow up about this quote on WhatsApp" is a simple way to cover it
- Give people a clear way to stop, and honour it. Meta recommends this, and it's good manners anyway

### A note on UK marketing rules
The ICO's guidance on direct marketing treats purely administrative or customer service messages differently from marketing, but says a message with any promotional element counts as direct marketing. A follow-up about the customer's own quote, with no offers, sits on the service side. A message offering a discount or advertising other work does not. If you're unsure about your wording, read the ICO's guidance or ask an adviser.

### What to automate and what stays personal
Task | Runs on its own | Stays with you
--- | --- | ---
Logging each quote sent (customer, job, price, date) | Yes, from your quoting tool or a form | Checking the details are right
Sending messages 1 to 3 on time | Yes, and stops when they reply | Approving the wording once
Spotting a reply | Yes, the chat is flagged for you | Reading it
Answering questions about the job or the price | No | Yes, always
Changing the price or the scope | No | Yes, always
A big job that's gone quiet | A reminder to call | The call itself
A weekly list of open, won and lost quotes | Yes | Deciding what to do about it

It's built on the tools you already use (your quoting or job software, Google Sheets, and your WhatsApp Business number where it can be connected), so there's nothing new to learn. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it. If AI drafts a reply to a customer, a person always approves it first.

### How many times should I chase a quote?
Three messages over about two weeks is a sensible default for most domestic jobs. After the third, stop. A customer who wants the job will come back, and one who's been chased five times usually won't.

### Should I follow up on WhatsApp or by text?
Use the channel the customer used to contact you. If they came in on WhatsApp, follow up there. If they phoned or emailed, a text or an email may feel less intrusive. The same sequence works on any of them.

## EICR remedial work follow-up for electricians: codes, 28 days and approvals
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/eicr-remedial-work-follow-up-electricians/

EICR remedial work follow-up means getting the landlord or letting agent to approve and book the C1, C2 and FI work on an unsatisfactory report before the legal deadline. In England, the Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 require the landlord to have that work done within 28 days starting with the date of the inspection, or sooner if the report says so. The duty is the landlord's, but a quick quote and a dated follow-up schedule make it far easier for them to meet it.

EICR remedial work follow-up is where many electricians who test rented homes lose time and jobs. The inspection is done, the report says unsatisfactory, and the remedial quote goes to a [letting agent](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/letting-agent-compliance-certificate-reminders/) who forwards it to a landlord who is on holiday. Meanwhile the 28 days are running. This page sets out the codes and the deadline as the regulations and the gov.uk guidance describe them, then gives you a follow-up workflow, a message template and a tracker you can copy. It covers England. Wales and Scotland have their own rules.

### EICR codes and what each one means for the landlord
The gov.uk guidance for landlords (published November 2025) uses these codes. A C1 or C2 means the report will say the installation is unsatisfactory for continued use. The guidance also says the inspector may make any C1 hazard safe before leaving.
Code | Meaning (gov.uk wording) | Must the landlord act?
--- | --- | ---
C1 | Danger present. Risk of injury | Yes, within 28 days or a shorter period in the report
C2 | Potentially dangerous | Yes, within 28 days or a shorter period in the report
FI | Further investigation required without delay | Yes, the investigation must be carried out in the same period
C3 | Improvement recommended | No. The guidance says C3 alone doesn't stop a report being satisfactory

### The 28-day deadline, and when it starts
Regulation 3(4) of the 2020 regulations says the landlord must make sure the further investigative or remedial work is carried out by a qualified person within 28 days, or within the period specified in the report if that is less, "starting with the date of the inspection and testing". So the clock starts on the day you test, not the day you send the report or the quote. Some summaries online are vaguer, so go by the regulation and by what your own report says. Once the work is done, regulation 3(5) says the landlord must get written confirmation from a qualified person and send it, with the report, to each tenant and to the local council within 28 days of completion. The gov.uk guidance lists a satisfactory EICR, an Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) or a Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate (MEIWC) as acceptable confirmation. If a landlord doesn't do the work, the council can serve a remedial notice, and the guidance says councils can impose a financial penalty of up to £40,000. Since the 2025 amendment, the same rules also apply to social landlords in England.

### Where remedial work stalls
- The report and the quote arrive in one long email, and the landlord reads the report but not the price
- The agent has to forward it, and the landlord's approval comes back to the agent, not to you
- Nobody writes down the deadline date, so everyone thinks there's more time than there is
- Approval comes, but booking access with the tenant takes another week
- The work is done, but the certificate sits in your van and the landlord can't send it on

### A follow-up workflow for remedial quotes
1. Inspection day: log the property, the inspection date, the codes found and the deadline date. Put the deadline a day or two early in your tracker, since the period starts with the inspection day itself.
2. Within 24 hours: send the report and a separate remedial quote to whoever instructed you. List each C1, C2 and FI item, its price, and the deadline date in plain words.
3. Day 3 after the inspection: if there's no approval, send the follow-up message below, by email or [on WhatsApp](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/whatsapp-quote-follow-up-tradespeople/).
4. Day 7: a second follow-up offering two dates for the work. If an agent instructed you, ask whether they need anything from you to get the landlord's answer.
5. Day 14: a final message stating the deadline date clearly and asking for a yes or no. Keep a dated copy of everything you sent.
6. On approval: book the work and arrange access with the tenant or agent the same day.
7. On completion: issue the EIC or MEIWC that day and send it to whoever instructed you, with a reminder that the landlord has 28 days from completion to send it to the tenants and the council.

### Remedial quote follow-up template
Follow-up email or message to the landlord or agent (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: [address]: EICR remedial work, approval needed by [date]

Hi [name],

Following the electrical inspection at [address] on [inspection date], the report found [number] items that need remedial work or further investigation ([codes, e.g. two C2 and one FI]). The quote for this work is attached: [amount].

Under the electrical safety regulations for rented homes in England, this work needs to be completed within 28 days of the inspection date, which means by [deadline date], or sooner if the report says so.

I can do the work on [date] or [date]. If you reply "approved" with your preferred date, I'll arrange access with the tenant and send the certificate as soon as the work is done.

If you'd like another electrician to do it, that's fine, just let me know so I can update my records.

Thanks,
[your name]
[business, phone]
```

### A remedial work tracker you can copy
One row per report. A shared Google Sheet is enough to start. For illustration only, with made-up addresses and dates:
Property | Inspection date | Codes | Deadline | Quote sent | Approved | Booked | Confirmation sent
--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Flat 2, 10 Example Road | 3 Nov | 2 x C2, 1 x FI | 30 Nov | 4 Nov | 7 Nov | 12 Nov | 12 Nov
14 Sample Street | 5 Nov | 1 x C1 (made safe), 1 x C2 | 2 Dec | 5 Nov | Chased 8 Nov |  | 

### What stays with you
Your coding, your quote and your professional judgement. A workflow can log the dates, send the follow-ups on time, stop when someone replies and show you which properties are close to their deadline. It doesn't decide what's dangerous or what the work costs, and if AI drafts a message to a landlord, a person always approves it first.

### How Mike Automations would build this
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how your reports and quotes go out today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your certification software's exports, your email, Google Sheets), so there's nothing new to learn. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### When do the 28 days start?
Regulation 3(4) says the period starts with the date of the inspection and testing. If your report gives a shorter period for an item, that shorter period applies.

### Does a C3 have to be fixed?
No. The gov.uk guidance says a C3 means improvement is recommended and doesn't stop a report being satisfactory. You can still quote for it, kept separate from the required work.

### Who sends the confirmation to the council?
The landlord, or their agent. The regulations put the duty on the landlord to send the written confirmation and the report to tenants and the council within 28 days of completion. You make that easy by sending the certificate promptly.

## Landlord approval limits for repairs: a ready policy for letting agents
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/landlord-repair-approval-limits/

A landlord approval limit for repairs is the amount a letting agent may spend on one repair without asking the landlord first, agreed in writing in the management agreement. Above the limit, the agent sends the landlord the quote with a deadline to reply, chases on a fixed schedule and logs the decision. Emergencies follow a separate rule that the landlord agrees in advance.

A landlord approval limit for repairs decides [how fast a tenant's repair gets done](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/letting-agent-maintenance-requests/). Without a clear limit, every job waits for an email reply, the tenant chases you, and you chase the landlord. With a vague one, you end up arguing about a bill after the work is done. This page gives you a policy you can agree with each landlord, a message to send when a job is over the limit, a chasing schedule for landlords who go quiet, and a simple log so every decision can be found later.

### What the limit is, and where it belongs
The limit is part of your agreement with the landlord, so put it in the management agreement or a signed schedule to it, not in an email thread. It covers what you may spend on one job without asking. It doesn't change who is responsible for repairs. In England, gov.uk's private renting guide (checked November 2026) says the landlord is always responsible for repairs to the structure and exterior, basins, sinks, baths and other sanitary fittings including pipes and drains, heating and hot water, gas appliances, pipes, flues and ventilation, electrical wiring, and fire safety issues. It also says tenants should report faults that could damage health straight away, and that the landlord should tell the tenant when to expect the repair. Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own standards and procedures, so check the local rules for properties there. A limit helps you meet those duties faster. It isn't legal advice, and it doesn't replace it.

### The approval policy: what to agree with each landlord
Agree these points once, at sign-up or at the next review, and record the answers against the property. The example column is for illustration only: the right numbers depend on the property, the landlord and your fees.
Policy item | What to decide | Example (for illustration)
--- | --- | ---
Standard limit | The most you can spend on one job without asking, and whether it includes VAT | £300 including VAT per job
Emergency rule | What you may do at once when a repair is urgent, and up to what amount | Make safe and fix up to £750, then tell the landlord the same day
Quotes | When you need more than one quote before asking for approval | Two quotes for jobs over £1,000
Reply window | How long the landlord has to reply to an approval request | 2 working days
No reply | What happens when the window passes with no answer | A phone call, then the emergency rule only if the job has become urgent
Contact order | Who to try, and how, when the landlord is unreachable | Email, then text, then a named second contact
Contractors | Whether you use your own contractors or the landlord's | The agency's usual contractors unless the landlord names one
Reporting | How the landlord hears about jobs under the limit | Listed on the monthly statement with the invoice

### What counts as urgent
Write the list down, because "urgent" is where most disputes start. Agree it with each landlord and keep it short. Common items to discuss:
- No heating or hot water, especially in winter or with a vulnerable tenant
- A suspected gas leak or a carbon monoxide alarm sounding (the tenant should call the gas emergency number first)
- Electrical faults that are a danger, such as exposed wiring or a burning smell
- A water leak that is spreading or coming through a ceiling
- A front door or window that won't lock
- No working toilet in the property

### Approval request template
Send this when a job is over the limit. Attach the quote and the tenant's photos so the landlord can decide from the message alone.
Email or message to the landlord:
```
Subject: Approval needed: [repair] at [property address]

Hi [landlord name],

Your tenant at [property address] reported [short description of the problem] on [date]. Photos are attached.

[Contractor name] has quoted £[amount] including VAT to [what the work is]. This is over your approval limit of £[limit], so we need your go-ahead before booking.

Please reply by [day and time] with one of these:
1. Approve: we book the work and let the tenant know.
2. Get another quote first.
3. You'll arrange the repair yourself (please tell us who and when, so we can update the tenant).

If we don't hear from you by then, we'll call you. If the problem becomes urgent before you reply, we'll act under the emergency rule in your management agreement and tell you straight away.

Thanks,
[your name], [agency name]
```

### Chasing a landlord who hasn't replied
Set the schedule once and follow it every time, so no request sits in an inbox for a week. This example uses a 2 working day reply window.
When | What happens | Who
--- | --- | ---
Day 0 | Approval request sent with the quote and photos. The tenant is told the job is waiting for the landlord's go-ahead | Workflow
Day 1 | A short reminder by email and text: "We still need your answer on [repair]" | Workflow
Day 2, end of the reply window | A phone call to the landlord. If there's no answer, the second contact is tried | A person in the office
Day 3 | The job goes on the manager's list with the full history, and the tenant gets an update | Workflow, then a person decides
Any time | If the problem becomes urgent, the emergency rule applies and the landlord is told the same day | A person in the office

### Logging every decision
If a landlord later questions a bill, the log is your answer. Keep one record per job, against the property, with:
- The tenant's report, the date it came in and the photos
- The quote or quotes, and the limit that applied on that date
- When approval was requested, each reminder and each call
- The landlord's answer, word for word, with the date and time
- Whether the job went ahead under the limit, with approval, or under the emergency rule
- The contractor's invoice and the date the tenant confirmed the repair was done

### How Mike Automations would build this
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how repairs and approvals run in your agency today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price. The workflow is built on the tools you already use (your email, a shared spreadsheet or drive, and your property management software where it allows a connection). It checks each job against that landlord's limit, sends the approval request, chases on your schedule, updates the tenant and keeps the log. A person in your office still makes every call on urgent jobs, and approves anything AI drafts before it's sent. Live in 2-3 days. It's [a fixed $2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### What should a landlord's repair approval limit be?
There's no set figure in law. It's a business agreement between you and the landlord. Base it on the property's age and size, the cost of common jobs in your area, and how involved the landlord wants to be. Review it at least once a year.

### Can we treat no reply as approval?
Only if the landlord has agreed to that in writing beforehand, for example in the management agreement. Otherwise silence is not approval. The safer route is a fixed chasing schedule plus an emergency rule for jobs that can't wait.

### What about urgent repairs when the landlord can't be reached?
Agree an emergency rule in advance: what counts as urgent and how much you may spend to make the property safe. Act under that rule and tell the landlord the same day, with photos and the invoice.

### Is this the same as an owner approval threshold?
Yes. US property managers usually call it an owner approval threshold or a maintenance limit. The idea and the workflow are the same.
