## MTD for Income Tax: a quarterly update workflow for UK practices
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/making-tax-digital-income-tax-practice-workflow/ (2026-11-10)

Under MTD for Income Tax, sole traders and landlords over the income threshold send HMRC a quarterly update from compatible software by 7 August, 7 November, 7 February and 7 May, then submit their tax return by 31 January. HMRC has said there are no penalties for late quarterly updates in the 2026 to 2027 tax year, but the updates are still required, and penalty points apply to them from 2027 to 2028. For a practice, the job is getting each client's records in before every 7th.

MTD for Income Tax (Making Tax Digital for Income Tax) started on 6 April 2026 for sole traders and landlords whose qualifying income was over £50,000. For most practices the hard part isn't the software. It's that [one annual chase for records](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/self-assessment-document-chasing/) has become four quarterly ones, for every client in scope.
Two deadlines have now passed: 7 August and 7 November 2026. The next is 7 February 2027, and the £30,000 group joins on 6 April 2027. Below: the rules to keep at hand, what to review after the first two quarters, and a workflow that stops each 7th turning into a pile of last-minute emails.

### Who is in scope, and when
MTD for Income Tax applies to sole traders and landlords registered for Self Assessment. HMRC decides who joins from qualifying income: total self-employment and property income before expenses (turnover), taken from an earlier tax return. Employment income, dividends, pensions and a share of partnership profit don't count. GOV.UK sets out three waves:
Joins MTD from | Qualifying income over | Decided by the tax return for
--- | --- | ---
6 April 2026 | £50,000 | 2024 to 2025
6 April 2027 | £30,000 | 2025 to 2026
6 April 2028 | £20,000 | 2026 to 2027

### Details that catch practices out
- HMRC writes to clients it finds over the threshold, but GOV.UK is clear that it's still the client's responsibility to check and sign up if no letter arrives.
- To sign up, the client must be registered for Self Assessment and have sent a tax return in the last 2 years.
- Clients still send a normal Self Assessment return for the tax year before they start. Your April 2027 joiners file their 2026 to 2027 return the old way.
- Some people are exempt, for example if they are digitally excluded. Exempt clients still report their income in a Self Assessment return.
- Partnerships will join later. HMRC says it will set out that timeline at a later date.
- HMRC checks qualifying income every year, so recheck clients just under a threshold after each return. Once in, a client can only opt out after 3 tax years in a row below the threshold.

### Quarterly update deadlines
Each quarterly update is a cumulative summary of income and expenses from 6 April to the end of the period, for each self-employment and property business. It isn't a tax return, and no accounting adjustments are needed. A nil update is still required if nothing happened in the period. HMRC lists two kinds of period. Clients whose accounting period runs 1 April to 31 March should use calendar periods, chosen in the software before the first update; the choice can't be changed for the rest of the tax year.
Standard period (6 April start) | Calendar period (1 April start) | Update deadline
--- | --- | ---
6 April to 5 July | 1 April to 30 June | 7 August
6 April to 5 October | 1 April to 30 September | 7 November
6 April to 5 January | 1 April to 31 December | 7 February
6 April to 5 April | 1 April to 31 March | 7 May (the following tax year)

### The tax return and penalties: what applies this year
Source: GOV.UK, "Penalties for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax", last updated 30 March 2026. Rules change, so check that page before you put penalty wording in a client letter.
- The tax return (older guidance calls it the final declaration) is still due by 31 January after the tax year ends, sent from MTD-compatible software. Quarterly updates don't replace it, and HMRC won't accept the return until the updates are in.
- For the 2026 to 2027 tax year, HMRC says there are no penalties for missing a quarterly update deadline. Penalty points still apply to a late tax return.
- From the 2027 to 2028 tax year, each missed quarterly update also earns a point. At 4 points the client gets a £200 penalty, and another £200 for each further missed deadline.
- Late payment penalties are new too: none in the first 15 days, then a percentage of the tax owed (3% for 2026 to 2027, 4% from 2027 to 2028), with 30 days' grace in a client's first year.
- The old penalties still apply to tax years before a client joined. An April 2026 joiner's 2025 to 2026 return, due 31 January 2027, is under the current rules.

### What to review after the first two quarters
The easement means a late update in 2026 to 2027 costs nothing in penalties, so it's tempting to let things slide. Use this year as a rehearsal instead: next year every missed 7th counts. Before 7 February, look at your April 2026 group and answer these questions:
1. Which clients sent records after the deadline for quarter 1 or quarter 2, and how many reminders did each one need?
2. Who has no bank feed connected, and so sends everything by hand?
3. Which clients sent a nil update or a partial one that will need correcting in the next update?
4. Is anyone on standard periods who should have chosen calendar periods?
5. Which of your 2027 joiners (qualifying income over £30,000 on their 2025 to 2026 return) are [authorised and signed up](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/mtd-income-tax-client-sign-up-tracker/), and which software will each use?

### A quarterly workflow that mostly runs on its own
1. Tag every client by MTD start date (2026, 2027, 2028, exempt or not in scope) and by period type, so each one gets the right messages on the right dates.
2. Pick one way in for records: bank feeds into the software where possible, and one upload link per client for everything else. No attachments scattered across inboxes.
3. About two weeks before each period ends, send a short reminder: what to record, and where to send anything the bank feed doesn't cover.
4. The day after the period ends, send each client a personal list of what's still missing, with the upload link. Set your own cut-off about 10 days before the 7th.
5. Remind on a fixed rhythm until the list is complete, then stop, and say thank you.
6. Give the team one daily view: complete, partial, no response, and days left until the 7th.
7. A week before the deadline, flag anyone who hasn't opened anything for a phone call. A person decides what happens next.

### A client letter you can adapt
Many practices send a short note setting out who does what each quarter. Agree the wording with your own terms of engagement first.
Subject: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: what we need from you each quarter:
```
Hi [first name],

From [6 April 2026 / 6 April 2027], HMRC needs a short update on your [self-employment / rental] income every three months, sent from approved software. We'll prepare and send these for you.

What we need from you:
- Keep your [bank feed connected / app up to date] so most transactions come through on their own.
- Each quarter, upload anything the bank feed doesn't show (cash takings, receipts, [letting agent statements]) here: [upload link]
- Please send everything by our cut-off dates: [28 July], [28 October], [28 January] and [28 April].

We'll send you a reminder before each cut-off, listing only what's still missing.

The usual tax return is still due by 31 January after the tax year ends, and we'll prepare it from the quarterly figures.

Any questions, just reply.

[your name]
```

### Where automation helps, and where it shouldn't
Reminders, personal lists, filing documents and the daily status list are what a workflow does well. The judgement calls stay with you: what counts as complete, how to categorise an odd expense, and when to pick up the phone. Anything sent in your name uses wording you approved, and if AI reads or sorts documents, a person checks the result. The update itself is still sent from your MTD-compatible software.
The same routine works for [VAT quarters](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/vat-quarter-records-chasing/) and the January Self Assessment chase. [Our free guide, 25 AI automations for accountants](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/guide/), has more ideas like it.

### How we would build it for you
It starts with a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how your quarterly chase works today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price. It's built on the tools you already use (your practice software, email and cloud storage, where they allow a connection) and is usually live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is $2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/) ($1,500 for the first 3 clients), and you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Do quarterly updates replace the Self Assessment return?
No. Quarterly updates are in-year summaries. The tax return is still needed after the year ends, by 31 January, and it's sent from MTD-compatible software.

### Is there a penalty for a late quarterly update in 2026 to 2027?
No. HMRC says there are no penalties for missing a quarterly update deadline in the 2026 to 2027 tax year. The updates are still required before the tax return can be sent, and from 2027 to 2028 each missed update earns a penalty point.

### Can the workflow send the update to HMRC?
The update is sent from MTD-compatible software by you or the client. The workflow handles everything around it: reminders, collecting records and tracking who's ready.

## A client onboarding checklist for small accounting firms (UK & US)
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/accounting-client-onboarding-checklist/ (2026-11-10)

A client onboarding checklist for a small accounting firm covers ten steps: engagement letter, intake form, identity and AML checks, professional clearance, authorisation with the tax authority, software and bank feed access, the first document request, deadlines in your practice software, data security records, and a welcome email. In the UK that means customer due diligence before work starts and authorisation through your HMRC agent services account; in the US, Form 8821 or Form 2848 and your written information security plan. Most steps can be triggered automatically, one after another, while the checks and decisions stay with a person.

A client onboarding checklist matters because a new client saying yes is where the real work starts: letters, forms, [ID checks](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/aml-client-id-checks-workflow/), authorisations, software access and the first batch of documents. Done by hand, onboarding is where details slip, and where a good first impression turns into three weeks of back-and-forth.
Below is a checklist with an owner and timing for each step, country notes for the UK and US, a welcome email you can copy, and a note on which steps can run without anyone typing.

### The checklist, with owner and timing
# | Step | Owner | When
--- | --- | --- | ---
1 | Engagement letter sent for e-signature, with the scope and fees agreed on the call | Partner approves, then automatic | Day 0
2 | Intake form: contact details, business details, tax references, year end, software used | Automatic, once the letter is signed | Day 0
3 | Identity and AML checks: documents through a secure link, then a person reviews | Client, then reviewer | Days 0 to 5
4 | Professional clearance request to the previous accountant | Team | Days 1 to 14
5 | Authorisation to act with the tax authority | Team and client | Days 1 to 10
6 | Access to the accounting software and bank feeds | Client | Days 1 to 7
7 | First document request: prior returns, last accounts, open letters from the tax authority | Automatic | Once checks are clear
8 | Client set up in practice software with deadlines and recurring tasks | Team, or automatic from the intake form | Week 1
9 | Data security: client added to your records of where their data is held | Team | Week 1
10 | Welcome email: who their contact is, how to send documents, what happens next | Automatic | When steps 1 to 3 are done

### UK notes
- AML: under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017, identity should normally be verified before the business relationship starts (regulation 30). Your supervisor's guidance decides what evidence is enough. Our AML client ID checks post covers this step in detail.
- Authorisation: GOV.UK says you get authorisation through your HMRC agent services account and related services, for example the digital handshake for MTD for Income Tax, Online Agent Authorisation for Corporation Tax, PAYE and CIS, and the paper form 64-8 for some services. Never use the client's own HMRC sign-in details.
- Clearance: ask the previous accountant for [professional clearance](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/professional-clearance-letter-template/) and any handover information. Our professional clearance letter template has wording you can use.
- Companies: if you'll file for the company at Companies House, check whether directors have verified their identity.

### US notes
- Authorisation: Form 8821 (Tax Information Authorization) lets you see the client's IRS information. Form 2848 (Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative) lets an eligible person represent the client before the IRS. Choose the one that matches the engagement.
- Data security: the IRS says federal law requires all professional tax preparers to create and implement a data security plan. IRS Publication 5708 is a template for a written information security plan (WISP). Onboarding is the moment to record where the new client's data will live and who can see it.
- Identity: collect documents through a secure link, not email attachments, and record who checked them.

### Where onboarding usually goes wrong
- The same details get typed into three systems, with three chances for a typo
- Nobody owns the follow-up, so a missing ID document is noticed a month later
- The client gets five separate emails and isn't sure which one matters
- Work starts before the AML checks or the authorisation are complete
- Deadlines aren't set up until the first one is close

### What to automate, and what to keep
Each step triggers the next. When [the engagement letter](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/engagement-letter-automation/) is signed, the intake form goes out; when the form is in, the client record, folder and ID request are created. You get a single list of onboardings in progress and what each one is waiting for.
Step | A workflow can | A person keeps
--- | --- | ---
Engagement letter | Draft it from your template, send for signature, chase until signed | The scope, the fee and the final check
Intake form | Send it the moment the letter is signed, copy answers into your systems | Spotting anything unusual
ID and AML | Request documents, remind, file them, set the review date | The review and the decision to accept
Authorisation | Send the client the instructions and track who has confirmed | Submitting the request
First documents | Send a personal list and remind until it's complete | Reading the prior-year return

### A welcome email you can copy
Subject: Welcome to [firm name]: what happens next:
```
Hi [first name],

Welcome aboard. Here's what happens over the next week or so:

1. Your engagement letter is signed. Thank you.
2. Please upload your ID documents here if you haven't yet: [secure upload link]
3. We'll ask [HMRC / the IRS] for permission to act for you. [You'll get a code or a form to approve. Please do it as soon as it arrives.]
4. Then we'll send a short list of the documents we need to get started.

Your contact is [name], on [email] or [phone]. For documents, always use the upload link above, so nothing gets lost in email.

[your name]
```

### For illustration
For illustration: a new client signs the engagement letter on Monday morning. Within minutes they get one email with an intake form and an upload link for their ID and last year's return. On Thursday the two items still missing get a polite reminder. On Friday your team sees the client marked "ready for review", with everything in one folder and the authorisation request already sent.

### How we would build it for you
It starts with a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you onboard clients today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price. It's built on the tools you already use (your practice software, e-signature tool, email and cloud storage, where they allow a connection) and is usually live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is $2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/) ($1,500 for the first 3 clients), and you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it. If you're not ready for that, [our free guide, 25 AI automations for accountants](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/guide/), is a good place to start.

### Do we need a client portal for this?
No. A portal helps, but a workflow can run on your email, your drive and your practice software. If you already use a portal, it can send clients there instead.

### Can the ID check itself be automated?
Collecting the documents and reminding clients can. Many firms use a specialist ID verification service for the check. The decision to accept a client stays with a person.

### Should AML checks be done before we start work?
In the UK, the Money Laundering Regulations 2017 say identity should normally be verified before the business relationship is established, with a narrow exception for low-risk cases where it's needed not to interrupt business. Check your supervisor's guidance.

## How to get clients to send their documents on time
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/get-clients-to-send-documents-on-time/ (2026-11-10)

To get clients to send documents on time, send each client a personal list of exactly what's missing, give them one upload link that works on a phone with no login, remind them on a fixed schedule that lists only what's still outstanding, and set an internal cut-off weeks before the official deadline. Put that cut-off in the engagement letter, and keep a daily list of complete, partial and silent clients so your calls go to the people who need one.

To get clients to send documents on time, fix the request, not the client. Late documents are rarely about bad clients. Usually the request was vague, it arrived at a busy moment, and sending the files was more effort than putting it off. Fix those three things and most of the chasing goes away.
Below are six habits that work for [Self Assessment in the UK](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/self-assessment-document-chasing/) and [individual returns in the US](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bookkeepers/), a schedule you can copy, and the point where it makes sense to let a workflow do the sending.

### 1. Send a personal list, not a generic request
"Please send your documents for the year" is easy to postpone because nobody knows where to start. "We still need your P60, the rental statement from your letting agent and the mortgage interest certificate" can be done in ten minutes. Build the list from last year's file, and update it as items arrive.
Ask about specifics wherever you can. "What was the £1,200 payment to J Smith on 3 March?" gets answered faster than "please explain your bank transactions".

### 2. Make sending the easy part
One link per client, that works on a phone, with no account to create. A photo of a receipt should be enough. Every extra step (log in, find the folder, rename the file) is a reason to do it later. If you already have a client portal, keep it, but don't let a forgotten password be the reason a P60 arrives in January. Our post on [client portals versus email](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/client-portal-vs-email-document-collection/) covers the trade-offs.

### 3. Remind on a schedule, and stop when it's done
Clients don't mind reminders; they mind irrelevant ones. Reminders should list only what's still missing, come at a steady rhythm (every 7 to 10 days, then weekly near your cut-off) and stop the moment the list is complete. A reminder that asks for something already sent loses trust fast.

### 4. Give them a reason and a date
Put your internal cut-off in every message, a few weeks before the official deadline, and say what it protects them from. In the UK, GOV.UK says online Self Assessment returns for 2025 to 2026 are due by 31 January 2027, and a late return gets an initial £100 penalty even if no tax is owed. In the US, most individual returns are due April 15 for calendar-year filers, according to the IRS. Those are concrete reasons, said calmly.

### 5. Put the cut-off in the engagement letter
A date agreed at the start is easier to hold than one announced in December. Many firms state a records cut-off in their engagement letter and say what happens if records arrive later: the return may be filed late, or a fee for urgent work may apply. Check any wording with your professional body or insurer. An outline:
Example clause outline (adapt and check before use):
```
Your records
To prepare your [tax return] on time, we need your complete records by [30 November] each year. We'll send you a list of what we need and reminders before that date.

If records arrive after [30 November], we will do our best to file on time but cannot guarantee it, and [an additional fee for urgent work of [amount] may apply].
```

### 6. Know who's missing what, every morning
If the only record of who still owes you documents is someone's memory, the chasing will always be late. A daily list lets the team spend their calls on the people who actually need one.
Status | What it means | What happens next
--- | --- | ---
Complete | Everything on the list has arrived | Reminders stop, thank-you sent, ready to prepare
Partial | Some items in, some missing | Reminder lists only what's left
Silent | Nothing opened or sent | Reminders continue, phone call 3 weeks before cut-off
Stuck | Client replied with a problem | A person picks it up the same day

### A schedule you can copy
For illustration. Pick dates that suit your workload. Our post on when to start chasing Self Assessment clients goes month by month for the UK.
When | UK Self Assessment (31 January) | US individual returns (April 15)
--- | --- | ---
First request | Late April to May, after the tax year ends on 5 April | Early January, as forms start to arrive
Reminders | Every 10 days through the summer | Every 7 to 10 days
Internal cut-off | End of November | Early to mid-March
Phone calls | Early November, to anyone silent | Late February, to anyone silent
Final notice | Early December | Mid-March, with an extension conversation if needed

### Putting it together
Each of these is simple; doing all of them by hand for every client is not. This is where a document collection workflow pays off: it builds the lists, sends the reminders, files what arrives and gives you the morning list. You keep the conversations. If you want the exact wording, our [document chasing email templates](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/document-chasing-email-templates/) cover every stage from first request to final notice.
For illustration: a practice with 150 Self Assessment clients sends personal lists in May. By October the morning list shows who is complete, who is partial and who is silent. The team spends November calling the silent ones, instead of emailing everyone.

### How we would build it for you
It starts with a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you collect documents today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price. It's built on the tools you already use (your practice software, email and cloud storage, where they allow a connection) and is usually live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is $2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/) ($1,500 for the first 3 clients), and you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it.

### How often should I remind clients about missing documents?
Every 7 to 10 days is a steady rhythm, moving to weekly near your cut-off. Each reminder should list only what's still missing and stop as soon as the client is complete.

### Should we charge a fee for late records?
Many firms include a fee for urgent work in their engagement letter and mention it only when needed. It works best as a clear, agreed term rather than a surprise.

### What if a client sends some documents but not all?
Thank them for what arrived and send a short list of only what's left, with the same upload link. Don't start the work until the list is complete unless you've agreed otherwise.

## Email templates for chasing client documents (copy and paste)
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/document-chasing-email-templates/ (2026-11-10)

Email templates for chasing client documents work best as a short sequence: a first request with a personal list and one upload link, a friendly reminder 7 to 10 days later, a "send what you have" nudge, a deadline reminder, a final notice that names the real deadline, and a thank-you that stops the chase. Every message should list only what's still missing, keep the same upload link and quote your internal cut-off, which sits weeks before the official deadline.

Good email templates for chasing client documents are short, specific and polite, and they always say exactly what's missing. Below are seven emails and [two text messages](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/text-or-whatsapp-clients-for-documents/) for a typical request cycle, with a timing table and UK and US wording for the deadline.
Replace the parts in [brackets], keep each message to what the client needs to do, and send them from your own address so replies come straight back to you.

### The sequence at a glance
# | Message | When to send | Stops if
--- | --- | --- | ---
1 | First request | Day 0 | Client is complete
2 | Friendly reminder | Day 7 to 10 | Client is complete
3 | Send what you have | Day 21, if nothing has arrived | Anything arrives
4 | Deadline reminder | 2 weeks before your cut-off | Client is complete
5 | Final notice | After your cut-off, before the official deadline | Client is complete
6 | Thank-you | The day the list is complete | Sent once
7 | Something doesn't apply | When a client replies that an item isn't relevant | Sent once

### 1. The first request
Subject: Your [tax year] documents: what we need:
```
Hi [first name],

It's time to get your [tax year] records together. Here's what we still need from you:

- [document 1]
- [document 2]
- [document 3]

You can upload everything here, from your phone or computer: [upload link]

If you can send it by [internal deadline], we'll have plenty of time to prepare your return before the deadline.

Thanks,
[your name]
```

### 2. The friendly reminder (7-10 days later)
Subject: Quick reminder: [N] items still to send:
```
Hi [first name],

Thanks for what you've sent so far. We're still waiting on:

- [missing item 1]
- [missing item 2]

Same link as before: [upload link]

If anything on the list doesn't apply to you this year, just reply and let me know.

[your name]
```

### 3. "Send what you have" (when nothing has arrived)
Some clients wait until they have everything, so nothing arrives at all. This one gives them permission to start.
Subject: No need to wait for everything:
```
Hi [first name],

No need to wait until you have every document. Send whatever you have now, even one or two items, and we'll get started and tell you exactly what's left.

Upload link: [upload link]

Thanks,
[your name]
```

### 4. The deadline reminder
Subject: [N] days until our deadline for your records:
```
Hi [first name],

A quick note that we need your remaining records by [internal deadline] to file on time. Still missing:

- [missing item]

Upload link: [upload link]

If something is holding you up, reply to this email and we'll work it out.

[your name]
```

### 5. The final notice
Name the real deadline and the real consequence, calmly. For [UK Self Assessment](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/self-assessment-document-chasing/), GOV.UK says the online return for 2025 to 2026 is due by 31 January 2027, and a late return gets an initial £100 penalty, even if there's no tax to pay. For [US individual returns](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bookkeepers/), the IRS deadline for calendar-year filers is April 15.
Subject: Action needed: your [tax year] return:
```
Hi [first name],

We still don't have [missing item], and the filing deadline is [31 January / April 15]. Without it we can't complete your return, which may mean a late filing penalty [(HMRC charges £100 as soon as a return is late)].

Please upload it today if you can: [upload link], or call us on [phone] so we can agree what to do.

[your name]
```

### 6. The thank-you (when everything is in)
Subject: Got everything, thank you:
```
Hi [first name],

That's everything we need. Thank you! We'll be in touch by [date] with your return to review.

[your name]
```

### 7. When a client says an item doesn't apply
Subject: Re: your documents:
```
Hi [first name],

Thanks for letting us know. I've taken [item] off your list. That leaves:

- [remaining item]

Same link as before: [upload link]

[your name]
```

### Two text messages
A short text often gets a faster response than a fourth email. Only text clients who have agreed to it, keep it free of anything promotional, and never ask for personal details or documents by text.
Text messages (a reminder, then a last nudge):
```
Reminder:
Hi [first name], it's [your name] at [firm]. We're still waiting on [N] items for your [tax year] return. Upload link: [upload link]. Thanks!

Last nudge:
Hi [first name], [firm] here. We need [missing item] by [date] to file your return on time. Upload here: [upload link], or reply and we'll call you.
```

### Tips that make templates work
Sending these by hand works for a handful of clients. For dozens, a workflow can fill in each client's list, send on schedule and stop on its own, using exactly the wording you approved. If you want the system behind the emails (lists, cut-offs, the morning status list), read our post on how to get clients to send documents on time.
- Always list only what's still missing. A reminder that asks for things already sent loses trust fast.
- Keep the same upload link in every email, so clients never wonder where to send things.
- Use an internal deadline a few weeks before the official one.
- Stop all reminders the moment a client is complete, then send the thank-you.
- Send from a person's name, not a no-reply address, so clients can answer with questions.

### How we would build it for you
It starts with a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you chase documents today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price. It's built on the tools you already use (your email, practice software and cloud storage, where they allow a connection) and is usually live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is $2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/) ($1,500 for the first 3 clients), and you pay only once it's running and you're happy with it. For more ideas, [our free guide, 25 AI automations for accountants](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/guide/), is a quick read.

### How many reminders should I send?
Four or five emails over the request cycle is typical: a first request, one or two reminders, a deadline reminder and a final notice. Each one should list only what's still missing, and all of them stop when the client is complete.

### Should I mention penalties in a chasing email?
Yes, but only in the final notice and in plain terms. For UK Self Assessment, a late online return gets an initial £100 penalty from HMRC. Stating the real consequence once is more effective than repeating it in every email.

### Can I text clients about missing documents?
Yes, if they have agreed to be contacted by text. Keep it short, include the upload link, and never ask for documents or personal details to be sent by text.

## 1099-NEC checklist for bookkeepers: the 2026 tax year
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/1099-season-checklist-bookkeepers/ (2026-11-10)

For the 2026 tax year, Form 1099-NEC is due to both the IRS and the contractor by Monday, February 1, 2027, because January 31 falls on a Sunday. The reporting threshold for nonemployee compensation is now $2,000 for payments made from January 1, 2026. A good 1099 checklist for bookkeepers starts in November: list each client's vendors, collect missing W-9s, then confirm totals in early January.

This 1099 checklist for bookkeepers covers the 2026 tax year: what changed, what to do each month from November to the deadline, and which parts are worth automating. Every January, bookkeepers find out which clients paid contractors all year without [collecting a W-9](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/w9-request-email-template/). The forms aren't hard. The missing names, addresses and tax IDs are. Most of that can be fixed in November and December, while vendors still answer email.

### Key dates and rules for the 2026 tax year
These come from the IRS Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC, the General Instructions for Certain Information Returns and the IRS e-file pages, all checked on irs.gov in November 2026. Confirm them again before you file, because the IRS updates its instructions during the season.
Rule | What it means for your clients
--- | ---
Deadline | 1099-NEC goes to the IRS and to the contractor by January 31. If that day is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the due date moves to the next business day. January 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so the deadline is Monday, February 1, 2027.
Threshold | The IRS says that for tax years beginning after 2025 the reporting threshold rose to $2,000 (it was $600) and may be adjusted for inflation from calendar year 2027. It applies to payments made from January 1, 2026.
E-filing | A business with 10 or more information returns in a year, counting W-2s and 1099s together, must file them electronically.
Free e-filing | The IRS's Information Returns Intake System (IRIS) is a free portal for e-filing 1099s. It needs a Transmitter Control Code, and the IRS says the application can take up to 45 days, so apply in November, not January.
Card and app payments | Payments made by credit card, debit card or through a payment app are reported by the payment company on Form 1099-K. They don't go on your client's 1099-NEC.
Corporations | Payments to corporations, including LLCs taxed as C or S corporations, generally don't need a 1099-NEC. Attorneys are the exception: legal fees of $2,000 or more are reported even when the law firm is incorporated.
Backup withholding | If a vendor doesn't give a correct taxpayer identification number (TIN), the payer may have to withhold 24% from future payments and send it to the IRS.

### The checklist, month by month
1. Early November: pull a vendor list for each client with year-to-date totals and the payment method for each vendor.
2. Mark the vendors likely to need a 1099-NEC: unincorporated contractors paid for services, likely to reach $2,000 by December 31, and paid by check, ACH or cash rather than by card or payment app.
3. Check which of them have a W-9 on file. For the rest, send a W-9 request now, with a secure way to return it.
4. If your clients will file 10 or more returns and you plan to use IRIS, apply for the Transmitter Control Code now.
5. Late November to December: remind the vendors still missing every week until the W-9 arrives. Tell the client which vendors haven't answered, so they can raise it at the next payment.
6. For foreign contractors, ask for the right Form W-8 instead of a W-9. The IRS instructions for Form W-9 point foreign persons to the W-8 series or Form 8233.
7. Early January: add December payments, re-check who crossed $2,000, and send the final list to each client to confirm.
8. Mid-January: prepare, review and file. Send copies to contractors by February 1, 2027.
9. After filing: set up W-9 collection at the point of first payment for every new vendor, so next January is lighter.

### A W-9 request you can copy
Send it from your client's name or from your firm on their behalf, whichever the client prefers. Keep it short. People ignore long emails about tax forms.
W-9 request email:
```
Subject: W-9 needed for [client business name] payments

Hi [vendor name],

Thanks for your work for [client business name] this year. To prepare year-end tax forms, we need a completed Form W-9 from you.

Please fill it in and upload it here: [secure upload link]

It takes about five minutes. Please don't send your tax ID by regular email.

Could you send it by [date, e.g. November 30]? If you've already sent one this year, just reply and let us know.

Thank you,
[name]
[firm name], on behalf of [client business name]
```

### Common mistakes that cause January rework
- Counting card and payment app payments toward the 1099-NEC total. Those belong on the payment company's 1099-K.
- Leaving out an incorporated law firm. Legal fees are the exception to the corporation rule.
- Using last year's $600 threshold, which sends forms to vendors who no longer need one.
- Accepting a W-9 as a plain email attachment. Ask for it through a secure upload link instead.
- Finding out in January that a TIN doesn't match. Payers who sign up can check name and TIN pairs through the IRS TIN Matching service before filing.

### What to automate, and what stays with you
The W-9 chase is a good job for a workflow, like the rest of [tax-season chasing for bookkeepers](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bookkeepers/). Each vendor gets a request with a secure form, reminders go out until it's back, the signed form is saved in the client's folder, and you get one list of who's still missing. If your clients are on QuickBooks Online, Intuit's help pages say it can scan the books for vendors who likely need a 1099, then prepare and e-file the forms as a paid service. The workflow fills the gap before that: getting the W-9s in.
You stay responsible for deciding who needs a form, checking the totals and signing off the filing. The workflow collects, reminds and reports.

### For illustration
For illustration: on November 15 each client gets a short list of vendors without a W-9. With the client's OK, every one of those vendors gets the request above with a secure link. Reminders go out each Monday. By mid-December you have a list of the three who never answered, and the client calls them before paying their next invoice.

We start with a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how you handle 1099 season today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every vendor without a W-9 gets a request by November 15 and reminders stop when it's uploaded".
